title: Seasonal Trainer, China Grove - Full Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Summary

The Core Trainer will assist with the on-boarding and job task-based training of Seasonal and Core Colleagues. The trainer should demonstrate knowledge of all job tasks within their assigned department and function and deliver a high-level of accuracy and consistency when performing the work, training colleagues, or reviewing completed work. Core Trainers will be crossed-trained in all areas of the facility. This role plays a critical part in developing colleagues through training, retraining and supporting both new and current team members to ensure operational excellence, accuracy and consistency. The Core Trainer demonstrates a deep understanding of the end- to- end supply chain flow and embodies the genuine hospitality and inclusive culture of Macy’s.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

What You Will Do

Training Support

  • Support Core and Seasonal Colleagues in assigned departments/functions by training and coaching on essential job tasks to ensure successful job performance.
  • Provide onboarding and operational training for new hires to ensure understanding of operating procedures, safety expectations, quality standards, and productivity goals.
  • Provide refresher training and retraining for existing colleagues who are not meeting operational performance, quality, safety, or productivity standards to reinforce proper operating procedures and improve overall performance.
  • Ensure work instructions, safety guidelines, and quality expectations are consistently followed throughout daily operations.
  • Consult and partner with designated Training Ambassador regarding work instructions, process updates, operational gaps, and training opportunities to ensure consistency and standardization across the facility.
  • Serve as a cross-functional trainer capable of supporting operational training needs across multiple departments throughout the facility.
  • Complete training checklists and conduct follow-up to ensure colleagues successfully complete the training period and achieve operational standards.
  • Perform frequent quality and productivity audits of work processed and provide immediate coaching and corrective feedback when needed.
  • Observe workflows, minimize errors, assess job proficiency, and retrain colleagues as necessary to improve performance and productivity.
  • Partner with Warehouse Managers and Leads to identify operational gaps, problem solve performance issues and implement training solutions that improve execution and productivity.
  • Demonstrate a passion for training and developing others while creating an engaging learning environment that motivates colleagues to succeed.
  • Adapt training methods to support different learning styles and operational demands.

Communication

  • Greet colleagues on their first day of employment and conduct orientation activities including building tours, time clock procedures, and reliability expectations.
  • Act as a point person for colleagues by answering questions related to processes, functions, safety, and operational expectations.
  • Communicate issues, concerns, and performance trends promptly to Managers, or Shift/Functional Directors for quick resolution.
  • Build positive working relationships and effectively influence and motivate others to drive accountability, engagement, and productivity.
  • Maintain strong attention to detail when documenting training progress, identifying performance trends, and communicating operational updates.

Safety Throughout Shift Safety Advocate

  • Demonstrate and reinforce safe workplace behaviors consistent with company safety policies and procedures.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Maintain regular, dependable attendance and punctuality.
  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships and ensures authentic connections with colleagues, customers, and communities.
  • Demonstrate flexibility to support changing business needs, peak operations, and cross-functional training initiatives.

Who You Are

Must be able to:

  • Strong attention to detail is essential to maintain quality, safety, and operational efficiency.
  • Understand and communicate effectively with, co-workers, leads, and facility leadership.
  • Read and understand employment policies and safety rules/procedures in English.
  • Demonstrate an affinity and passion for training, coaching, and developing others.
  • Exhibit strong attention to detail and the ability to consistently reinforce standard operating procedures.
  • Motivate, influence, and engage colleagues to achieve operational productivity and quality goals.
  • Partner effectively with Warehouse Managers, Training Ambassadors and Leads to resolve operational challenges and improve team performance.
  • Demonstrate strong interpersonal, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Positively impact team success in a fast-paced environment.
  • Manage multiple priorities and processes effectively while maintaining operational standards.
  • Work assigned scheduled including days, evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.

Essential Physical Requirements You Will Perform

  • This position requires lifting, constant moving, standing, and reaching with arms and hands.
  • Involves standing for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 50lbs., stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders.
  • Reaching, including above eye level, crouching, kneeling, and stooping.
  • Involves close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment.
  • Frequent use of computers and other technology, necessary to perform job functions, including handheld equipment.

Supply Chain Only and Colleagues Working in a Supply Chain Facility except in locations governed by a Collective Bargaining Agreement:

Random drug testing for all colleagues will be conducted on a monthly or semi-monthly basis, depending upon factors including but not limited to the size of the facility and the number of colleagues on roll. Colleagues will be randomly selected for testing by a third party. Testing must be completed on the same workday the colleague is informed of selection for testing, absent extenuating circumstances. In all circumstances, testing must be completed within 24 hours of notification.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!

title: At Your Service Center Associate, Makalapua - Part Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As an At Your Service Center Colleague, you are at the heart of delivering a seamless and personalized shopping experience. You’ll support all At Your Service activities, including Buy Online Pickup In Store (BOPS), merchandise returns, order pickups, and other assigned tasks - all while upholding Macy’s service standards.

This role requires strong multitasking abilities, problem-solving, attention to detail, and a customer-first mindset. You’ll thrive in a fast-paced environment where flexibility is key, including working a variety of shifts such as nights, weekends, and holidays.

This role goes far beyond just being a cashier. Here, the customer is at the heart of everything we do - every day, all day. If you're passionate about selling, reaching goals, working as a team, and creating amazing experiences through genuine hospitality, this could be the perfect fit for you! You’ll also help keep the shopping space clean, organized, and inviting so every customer feels welcome the moment they walk in.

How Our At Your Service Colleagues Spend Their Day…

  • Every day starts with a positive example. As an At Your Service Colleagues (AYS), you come in energized and ready to make an impact - wearing your name badge with pride, greeting teammates with warmth, and helping ensure the At Your Service areas is clean, organized, and ready for customers. You help set the pace by reviewing sales goals, learning about new arrivals and top-selling items, and staying up to date on trends and promotions - so you’re prepared to support the team and engage customers confidently.
  • In the At Your Service area, you lead through action - welcoming customers with genuine hospitality, making eye contact, and starting friendly, personal conversations that build lasting relationships. Assist customers in all aspects of total store fulfillment, including By Online and Pick Up in Store, be proficient in all systems needed to complete transactions, and ensure the collection area is organized so the customer pick-up experience is friction-free
  • You help maintain a shoppable space by recovering merchandise and keeping the pickup and return areas clean while ensuring timely completion and curbside delivery of Buy Online Pickup In Store (BOPS) orders.
  • They always Finish Strong - sharing our Loyalty program benefits, making sure customers have all they need, and ending with a sincere thank-you, often walking the package around and using the customer’s name.
  • We believe service starts with each other - supporting one another with honesty, care, and collaboration so we can better serve our customers and communities.
  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. Who You Are

  • Flexible availability, including days, evenings, weekends and holidays with regular, dependable attendance and punctuality
  • Must be able to:
    • Understand and communicate effectively with customers, co-workers, and supervisors
    • Read and understand employment policies and safety rules/procedures in English
  • Makes prompt, sound decisions in real time to effectively address customer needs and resolve issues
  • Be comfortable communicating and collaborating with customers and colleagues
  • Meeting daily sales goal challenges
  • Responsible for acquiring new customers by opening credit accounts and sharing loyalty benefits
  • Enjoy meeting people, learning about them, and sharing information
  • Resourceful and eager to start a new venture and can adapt to changing priorities; you can work on your own but are great with team dynamics
  • You can handle electronic devices with no problem

Essential Physical Requirements You Will Perform

  • This position requires talking, lifting, constant moving, standing, and reaching with arms and hands.
  • Standing for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 25lbs. stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders, reaching, including above eye level.
  • Requires close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment.
  • Frequent use of computers and other technology, necessary to perform job functions, including handheld equipment, cash register and ability to process register transactions.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

title: DRE Assistant (In Office)
description:
Who We Are

Join a team that puts its People First! Since 1889, First American (NYSE: FAF) has held an unwavering belief in its people. They are passionate about what they do, and we are equally passionate about fostering an environment where all feel welcome, supported, and empowered to be innovative and reach their full potential. Our inclusive, people-first culture has earned our company numerous accolades, including being named to the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® list for eleven consecutive years. We have also earned awards as a best place to work for women, diversity and LGBTQ+ employees, and have been included on more than 50 regional best places to work lists. First American will always strive to be a great place to work, for all. For more information, please visit www.careers.firstam.com.

What We Do

The DRE Assistant supports the Subdivision Services DRE team in obtaining California Department of Real Estate (DRE) Final Public Reports for subdivision projects. This position assists with the preparation, organization, submission, and tracking of documentation required by the DRE and other regulatory agencies. Working under the supervision of the Department Manager, the DRE Assistant helps ensure projects are processed efficiently, accurately, and in accordance with company standards, client expectations, and regulatory requirements.

What You'll Do

  • Establish, organize, and maintain project files according to departmental procedures and processor direction.
  • Request agency letters, reports, and supporting documentation required for DRE applications and public report processing.
  • Assist in the preparation of DRE application forms and supporting documentation, excluding management documents and budgets.
  • Organize, assemble, copy, scan, and prepare application packages, responses, and supporting documentation for submission to regulatory agencies as provided by, or directed by, DRE Processor.
  • Follow all department policies, procedures, and quality standards.· Stay informed of new DRE regulations, policies, forms, and procedural changes affecting subdivision processing.
  • Communicate potential issues, delays, or concerns to management promptly to support proactive problem-solving and maintain client satisfaction.
  • Assist with the distribution of public reports upon issuance and support department workflow to meet client deadlines and schedules.
  • Support company and subdivision manager policies, programs, and objectives.
  • Participate in training programs, seminars, and continuing education opportunities as assigned.
  • Assist in mentoring and supporting team members to promote professional growth and departmental success.
  • Perform additional duties and special projects as needed to ensure timely and successful completion of client projects.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Real estate or related experience.
  • Strong organizational and administrative skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and PDF management software.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
  • Ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in subdivision processing, real estate, title, escrow, land development, regulatory compliance, or related fields.
  • Familiarity with California Department of Real Estate (DRE) procedures, applications, and public report requirements.
  • Experience handling regulatory filings and document management systems.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • Ability to prioritize workload and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Professional and client-focused approach to service.
  • Effective problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information appropriately.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and a collaborative work style.
  • Commitment to continuous learning and professional development.
** Note that the following statements only apply to candidates who will be working from an unincorporated area within Los Angeles County. **
First American will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws (e.g., the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act). title: Principal Network Engineer, Cloud Networking
description:
Job Summary

NetApp is seeking a hands-on Principal Engineer to lead cloud networking architecture and reliability for Google Cloud NetApp Volumes (GCNV), a Google first-party service built on NetApp virtual storage and cloud platform technologies. This is a high-impact role focused on preventing repeat network-driven customer impact while strengthening engineering depth across the SRE organization.

You will own technical direction for network infrastructure and hardening across regions and deployment stamps, including fabric design, routing and subnet integrity, reachability, connectivity, and topology-aware automation. You will also serve as a senior escalation point for critical incidents, lead operational readiness reviews, and partner across NetApp and Google to deliver secure, resilient cloud services at scale.

As a Principal Engineer, your responsibilities will include:

  • Lead network architecture, fabric design, and hardening across multi-region cloud environments, deployment stamps, subnets, and routing domains.
  • Design and implement network and fabric changes, connectivity guardrails, reachability audits, and topology-aware placement and routing automation.
  • Set technical direction and architecture standards for SRE and cloud platform teams, and lead design and operational readiness reviews for new regions, stamps, and releases.
  • Act as a senior escalation point during P0/P1 incidents; lead network-focused troubleshooting and drive root-cause analyses through durable corrective actions.
  • Partner with Product Engineering, Support, Google, and other stakeholders to resolve cross-team dependencies and improve service reliability.
  • Reduce operational toil and alert noise through automation, stronger observability, and preventive engineering controls.
  • Mentor engineers and raise the technical bar through code, architecture, and design reviews.
  • Contribute to roadmap and capacity planning, and represent the organization in technical forums with partners and customers.

Job Requirements

  • A minimum of 12 years of applicable professional experience in network engineering, cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, site reliability engineering, or a related field is required.
  • Deep hands-on experience designing and operating large-scale cloud or data center networks, including routing, subnet architecture, network fabrics, reachability, and multi-region connectivity.
  • Experience supporting production services on Google Cloud, AWS, or Microsoft Azure; Google Cloud experience is strongly preferred.
  • Proficiency with network automation and infrastructure-as-code using technologies such as Python, Go, Terraform, Ansible, Bash, Kubernetes, or CI/CD pipelines.
  • Demonstrated experience leading response to critical production incidents, performing root-cause analysis, and implementing preventive corrective actions.
  • Strong understanding of network security and hardening, observability, service reliability, failure domains, and operational readiness.
  • Experience setting architecture direction and influencing multiple engineering teams without direct authority.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical decisions clearly to engineering teams, partners, customers, and senior stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with BGP, VXLAN/EVPN, software-defined networking, Kubernetes/container networking, or cloud interconnect technologies.
  • Experience building or operating storage, infrastructure, or other highly available services across multiple regions.
  • Experience working with hyperscaler engineering teams or delivering a first-party cloud service.
  • Experience improving service placement, routing, capacity, or network topology through automation and data-driven guardrails.

Education

A bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a related field is a plus, but not required. Applicable education, certifications, and/or technical training are also valued. Additional relevant professional experience will be equally considered.

Compensation:
The target base salary range for this position is $225,000-$270,000 (Raleigh, NC Range) The salary offered will be determined by the candidate's location, qualifications, experience, and education and may be outside of this range. Final compensation packages are competitive and in line with industry standards, reflecting a variety of factors, and include a comprehensive benefits package. This may cover Health Insurance, Life Insurance, Retirement or Pension Plans, Paid Time Off (PTO), various Leave options, Performance-Based Incentives, employee stock purchase plan, and/or restricted stocks (RSU’s), with all offerings subject to regional variations and governed by local laws, regulations, and company policies. Benefits may vary by country and region, and further details will be provided as part of the recruitment process.

At NetApp, we embrace a hybrid working environment designed to strengthen connection, collaboration, and culture for all employees. This means that most roles will have some level of in-office and/or in-person expectations, which will be shared during the recruitment process.

Equal Opportunity Employer:

NetApp is firmly committed to Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and to compliance with all federal, state and local laws that prohibit employment discrimination based on age, race, color, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, religion, disability or genetic information, pregnancy, protected veteran status, and any other protected classification.

Why You'll Thrive at NetApp

At NetApp, you won't wait for the perfect moment—you'll make it. The early planning, the extra thought, the bold idea that turns good into great: That's how our people operate and how we continue to push the boundaries of data infrastructure.

NetApp is the trusted partner for organizations transforming data into opportunity. As the only enterprise-grade storage service natively embedded in Google Cloud, AWS, and Microsoft Azure, we empower customers to run everything from traditional workloads to enterprise AI with unmatched performance, resilience, and security.

Our culture

We celebrate mold breakers, bold thinkers, and problem solvers. We reward initiative, impact, and ownership. We provide flexibility so you can balance professional ambition with your personal life. Here, differences are not just welcomed—they drive everything we do.

If you're ready to innovate, rise to the challenge, and own every moment - make your next move your best one. Apply now.

title: Beauty Brand Expert - Elizabeth Arden, La Plaza Mall - Full Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As a Beauty Brand Expert at Macy’s, you are the go-to authority for your assigned brand, responsible for driving sales, elevating the customer experience, and leading with passion, expertise, and style. You serve as both a product educator and beauty enthusiast - creating personalized routines, demonstrating new trends, and helping customers look and feel their best.

In this role, you’ll inspire teamwork, coach fellow Beauty Advisors, and lead by example through exceptional service and product knowledge. You’ll foster customer loyalty, build relationships through clienteling, and execute brand strategies, events, and training in collaboration with store leadership and vendor partners. With a deep understanding of your brand and strong business acumen, you’ll analyze sales data, identify opportunities, and deliver results in a fast-paced, goal-driven environment.

How Our Beauty Brand Expert Leaders Spend Their Day…

  • Every day starts with a positive example. As a Beauty Brand Expert Leader, you come in energized and ready to inspire your team - wearing your name badge with pride, greeting colleagues with genuine warmth, and ensuring your counter is polished, organized, and fully prepared to welcome customers. You set the tone by reviewing daily sales goals, staying informed on new launches, top-performing products, and current beauty trends - so you're equipped to lead with confidence, support your team, and deliver exceptional service to every customer.
  • On the floor, you lead through action - welcoming customers with genuine hospitality, making eye contact, and starting friendly, personal conversations that build lasting relationships.
  • You help maintain a shoppable space by ensuring testers are clean and well-stocked, signage and pricing are current, and displays reflect brand standards. You lead by example, jumping in to support merchandising updates and keeping the space visually appealing and welcoming throughout the day.
  • You help the team Finish Strong - by reminding them to share Loyalty benefits, making sure customers leave with everything they need, and ending each interaction with a sincere thank-you, often using the customer’s name and adding a personal touch.
  • You know that service starts with each other. You model collaboration, honesty, and care - supporting your peers so the whole team can better serve our customers and communities.
  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

Who You Are and What You Will Do

  • Deliver exceptional customer service through personalized consultations and expert product knowledge
  • Build lasting relationships with clients and drive client development through outreach and follow-up
  • Review and analyze business performance of daily, weekly, monthly, seasonal, and annual sales results and implement strategies to grow business and improve results
  • Plan and execute in-store and vendor-led events to drive traffic and engagement
  • Maintain brand standards through proper merchandising, hygiene, and stock replenishment
  • Collaborate with vendors, personal stylists, and store leadership to optimize outcomes
  • Resolve customer concerns in a professional and customer-first manner
  • Stay informed on new launches, best-sellers, and beauty trends to support team education
  • Manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment with strong attention to detail
  • Demonstrate sound judgment, and a passion for the beauty industry
  • Responsible for acquiring new customers by opening credit accounts and sharing loyalty benefits
  • 3–5 years of relevant retail, beauty, or leadership experience preferred
  • Flexible availability, including days, evenings, weekends and holidays with regular, dependable attendance and punctuality
  • Must be able to:
    • Understand and communicate effectively with customers, co-workers, and supervisors
    • Read and understand employment policies and safety rules/procedures in English

Essential Physical Requirements You Will Perform

  • This position requires talking, lifting, constant moving, standing, and reaching with arms and hands
  • Standing for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 25lbs., stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders, reaching, including above eye level
  • Requires close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment
  • Frequent use of computers and other technology, necessary to perform job functions, including handheld equipment, cash register and ability to process register transactions

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!

title: Advancement Summer Internship Program - Corporate & Community Development / Children’s Miracle Network Intern
company: University of Iowa Center for Advancement
description:
The University of Iowa Center for Advancement (UICA) is currently providing opportunities for full- time paid summer internships. UICA encourages students from all backgrounds to explore careers in nonprofit settings, promote engagement with the University of Iowa, support and advance the university and its programs through meaningful pre-professional opportunities, and support potential graduates to obtain roles within our organization.

The UICA will provide 9 intern opportunities that provide 10 weeks of work experience, June 1 - August 6. Internships are open to students entering their second year of college in Fall 2027 through students graduating from any college or university in 2027. Interns will earn $18/hour and will be provided with the flexibility and technology to work from home two days per week if desired. Up to five unpaid vacation days will be available throughout the internship program if desired. At the conclusion of the internship, all interns are expected to give a final presentation highlighting their experience and projects they have worked on. Housing and benefits are not available as part of the intern experience and interns must be within driving distance of our Iowa City, IA office.

As the Corporate & Community Development/Children's Miracle Network Intern, you will support fundraising and donor engagement efforts for University of Iowa Health Care Stead Family Children's Hospital through Corporate and Community Development and Children's Miracle Network programs. Working alongside advancement professionals, you will help strengthen relationships with corporate partners, media partners, community supporters, and fundraising programs that directly benefit pediatric patients and their families. This internship will provide hands-on experience in corporate fundraising, cause marketing, event planning, community engagement, donor stewardship, and nonprofit partnership development while offering meaningful opportunities to support initiatives that advance children's health care.

Core Responsibilities

  • Coordinated corporate fundraising campaigns, including Dairy Queen Miracle Treat Day and Walmart initiatives, supporting partner engagement and revenue growth.
  • Managed corporate partner communications, campaign logistics, and project execution to strengthen relationships and maximize fundraising outcomes.

title: Senior Medical Coding Specialist
description:
Join Care Synergy and be part of a mission-driven organization dedicated to elevating care, advancing wellness, and strengthening the communities we serve. Our collaborative, supportive team works across hospice, palliative care, PACE, CAPABLE, and community-based wellness services to advance excellence for patients, participants, families, and those who care for them—all while offering excellent benefits and meaningful opportunities to grow and make an impact.

Care Synergy is looking for a Senior Medical Coding Specialist.

LOCATION: Denver, CO

STATUS: Full-time

SCHEDULE: Monday-Friday; 8am-5pm

PAY RANGE: $71,489 - $83,990

SUPPLEMENTAL PAY: Based on position, schedule and/or availability: Paid Mileage/Shift Differentials/Stipends/Overtime

CULTURE, BENEFITS AND PERKS:

  • We value engagement, community, and outreach initiatives and know it matters for our team members and our patients. We provide welcoming and supportive care to our patients and a work environment where all team members feel respected and valued.
  • We support a culture of work-life balance and provide team members with two, free, confidential and robust benefit programs designed to provide solutions to the logistical and financial problems that arise in life.
  • Employer pays over 90% of employee medical premium in some plans
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) with significant Employer Funding: Single $1,000, Family $2,000
  • Healthcare Benefits are effective on the 1st of the month following 30 days of employment
  • Extensive Paid Time Off (PTO/Vacation Pay): 18 days in the first year for FT team members
  • Seven Paid Holidays with an additional Floating Holiday
  • 403(b) Retirement Plan with Employer Match: 50% match up to 8% of total compensation
  • Company-Paid Life and AD&D Insurance
  • Career & Logo wear
  • Education Reimbursement Program
  • Clinical Career Ladders
  • Certification Pay
  • Generous Discover-a-Star Team Member Referral Program
  • Team Member Service Awards
  • Early Wage Access
  • Legal and Identity Protection
  • Robust Leadership Development Training Programs

WHY CARE SYNERGY?

Care Synergy is a Colorado-based nonprofit healthcare organization providing shared services and specialized expertise to Affiliates delivering compassionate care throughout the Front Range.

Our Affiliates serve individuals and families through hospice, palliative care, PACE, and other community-based programs. Behind that care is a dedicated team of professionals working together to strengthen quality, compliance, and operational effectiveness.

At Care Synergy, your expertise matters. You'll be part of a collaborative organization where your work contributes to the financial sustainability and quality of programs that make a meaningful difference in our communities.

THE DIFFERENCE YOU’LL MAKE

As our Enterprise Medical Coding Specialist, you'll play an important role in ensuring clinical documentation is accurately translated into appropriate medical codes, supporting regulatory compliance, reliable reporting, and appropriate reimbursement.

You'll work across three distinct areas of healthcare, partnering with providers, clinical leaders, Health Information Management (HIM), Compliance, and Revenue Cycle teams to improve coding accuracy and strengthen documentation practices.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

    • Review clinical documentation and assign accurate ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes for Hospice, Palliative Care, and PACE services.
    • Ensure coding accurately reflects documented diagnoses and complies with CMS, payer, and applicable regulatory requirements.
    • Support hospice coding, including principal and additional diagnoses, admissions, recertifications, and diagnosis updates.
    • Review palliative care encounters and apply appropriate diagnosis and encounter coding, including CPT and HCPCS codes when applicable to assigned professional services.
    • Support PACE diagnosis coding, including Medicare risk adjustment and hierarchical condition category (HCC) requirements.
    • Partner with physicians, nurse practitioners, and clinical teams to clarify documentation and resolve coding discrepancies.
    • Identify documentation gaps, coding trends, and opportunities to improve accuracy and consistency.
    • Collaborate with Revenue Cycle to resolve coding-related claim edits, denials, and reimbursement concerns.
    • Participate in coding audits, quality reviews, and process improvement initiatives.
    • Serve as a trusted coding resource, helping educate clinical teams on documentation and coding best practices.

WHAT YOU'RE GOING TO LOVE:

  • Meaningful work. Your expertise supports programs that care for individuals with serious illnesses, older adults, and families throughout Colorado.

  • Variety in your day. You'll work across Hospice, Palliative Care, and PACE, applying your knowledge to different clinical specialties and coding requirements.

  • Collaboration that matters. You'll partner with experienced clinical, compliance, HIM, and revenue cycle professionals who value accuracy, integrity, and teamwork.

  • An opportunity to make an impact. You'll help strengthen enterprise coding practices, improve documentation quality, and contribute to processes that support sustainable, high-quality care.

  • A mission-driven environment. You'll be part of a nonprofit healthcare organization where the work behind the scenes is just as important to our mission as the care delivered directly to patients and families.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED:

Required Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Current Certified Coding Specialist (CCS), Certified Professional Coder (CPC), or Certified Coding Specialist–Physician-based (CCS-P) credential.
  • Minimum three years of professional medical coding experience.
  • Strong knowledge of ICD-10-CM coding guidelines, medical terminology, and clinical documentation requirements.
  • Experience reviewing electronic medical records and assigning accurate diagnosis codes.
  • Understanding of Medicare coding and documentation requirements.
  • Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Effective communication skills and a collaborative approach to working with clinical and administrative teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate degree in Health Information Management, Health Information Technology, or a related field.
  • Experience with hospice, palliative care, PACE, or other community-based healthcare services.
  • Knowledge of Medicare risk adjustment and HCC coding.
  • Experience with professional services coding, including CPT and HCPCS.
  • Experience supporting coding audits, documentation improvement, or coding-related denial resolution.
  • Familiarity with electronic health record systems and coding software.

Care Synergy is a network of mission driven, nonprofit healthcare organizations dedicated to caring for very ill, frail, and primarily elderly individuals by keeping them at home and out of the hospital while maximizing comfort, dignity, and quality of life.

The Care Synergy enterprise includes a group of collaborating nonprofit Affiliates across Colorado’s Front Range that share resources, expertise, and infrastructure to deliver high quality, compassionate care. Collectively, the enterprise generates approximately $100 million in annual revenue and serves thousands of individuals and families each year through hospice, home health, palliative care, CAPABLE, wellness, and PACE programs.

Across the Care Synergy network, the organizations provide significant community impact, including more than 7,000 hospice patients served annually, more than 2,000 palliative care patients, more than 355,000 hospice days of care each year, and more than $1.6 million in charitable care provided annually.

Care Synergy affiliated programs include The Denver Hospice, Pathways Hospice, Pikes Peak Hospice and Palliative Care, Colorado Visiting Nurse Association, CAPABLE, and Superior Medical Equipment, along with PACE programs including Colorado PACE and Pathways PACE.

title: Senior Solution Architect in Melbourne with ability to obtain baseline clearance
description:
Senior Solution Architect

Melbourne | Hybrid | Australian citizenship required | Must be able to obtain Baseline clearance

Join Seers Digital and lead solution architecture for a major digital transformation supporting a major federal government client.

About Seers Digital

Seers Digital is an Australian technology consulting company delivering digital transformation, cloud, integration, automation and AI solutions. We work with major state and federal government agencies and organisations across banking, finance, construction and utilities.

Our teams combine technical expertise with a practical, collaborative approach to solving complex business challenges.

About the role

We are seeking an experienced Senior Solution Architect to lead the end-to-end architecture and design of a digital ordering and payment platform.

Working closely with program leadership, project management, service design and business analysis specialists, you will translate user and business requirements into secure, accessible and supportable solutions. Your work will guide platform selection, procurement, implementation and transition to operational support.

This role combines architecture leadership with practical delivery oversight across applications, integrations, data, identity, payments, hosting and security.

What you’ll do

  • Define the target architecture, solution boundaries, design principles and delivery roadmap.
  • Lead solution design across digital portals, workflows, integrations, data, identity and access, payments, notifications, reporting and operational support.
  • Assess existing Microsoft 365 and Power Platform solutions, identifying opportunities for reuse, migration and staged delivery.
  • Translate service blueprints, user journeys and business requirements into architecture models, technical specifications and clear design decisions.
  • Define measurable requirements for security, privacy, accessibility, performance, availability, resilience and supportability.
  • Design APIs, information flows and integrations with enterprise platforms and external service providers, including error handling, reconciliation and monitoring.
  • Establish secure authentication, authorisation and role-based access for internal and external users handling sensitive information.
  • Evaluate platform options and present recommendations covering cost, risk, scalability, interoperability and whole-of-life value.
  • Prepare architecture documentation, technical requirements and evaluation criteria to support procurement and supplier selection.
  • Provide technical leadership through design reviews, implementation, testing, migration, deployment and operational handover.
  • Collaborate with cyber security, privacy, finance, records, operations and assurance stakeholders to resolve design issues.
  • Communicate architecture recommendations and trade-offs clearly to technical teams, senior stakeholders and governance forums.

What you’ll bring

  • Extensive solution architecture experience across complex digital transformation programs, preferably within Australian federal or state government.
  • Demonstrated architecture leadership on at least two complex transactional, digital or workflow solutions, from discovery through implementation or operational transition.
  • Strong experience designing applications, integrations, data flows, identity services and secure access controls.
  • Experience delivering solutions with multiple enterprise or external service integrations using APIs, events, messaging or controlled data exchange.
  • Demonstrated understanding of the Australian Government Architecture and Digital Experience Policy.
  • Experience defining and assuring non-functional requirements, including accessibility, security, privacy, resilience and data residency.
  • Strong architecture documentation, options analysis and design governance skills.
  • Experience supporting procurement, platform assessment and vendor evaluation.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement, consultation and communication skills, with the ability to build agreement on complex design decisions.

Experience that will be well regarded

  • Microsoft Azure, Power Platform, Microsoft 365, identity services, API management, payment gateways and SaaS platforms.
  • Government services, legal technology or regulated environments handling sensitive information.
  • Digital ordering portals, payment workflows and financial controls.
  • Modular architecture, configurable business rules and staged integration with future enterprise platforms.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications or architecture certifications, such as TOGAF or Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert.

Why join Seers Digital?

  • Work on meaningful projects: Help modernise government services and improve how people access and use essential digital platforms.
  • Have a direct impact: Take ownership of important architecture decisions and guide solutions from early discovery through to delivery.
  • Collaborate with experienced people: Work alongside architects, developers, business analysts, service designers and delivery leaders who share knowledge and solve problems together.
  • Join a supportive team: Receive a welcoming induction, buddy support and access to colleagues across our consulting and delivery teams.
  • Broaden your experience: Build your expertise through Seers’ work across government and industry, spanning cloud, integration, digital platforms, automation and AI.
  • Stay connected: Be part of a collaborative consulting culture with opportunities to share ideas, contribute to better delivery practices and connect through team events.
  • Work in a hybrid environment: Combine onsite collaboration in Melbourne with work-from-home arrangements agreed with the client.

Location and eligibility

  • Applicants must live in Melbourne and be available for regular onsite attendance.
  • Hybrid arrangements are subject to client requirements and approval.
  • Applicants must be Australian citizens and able to obtain Baseline security clearance.
  • A National Police Check and relevant pre-employment screening will be required.

title: Advancement Summer Internship Program - Stewardship Intern
company: University of Iowa Center for Advancement
description:
The University of Iowa Center for Advancement (UICA) is currently providing opportunities for full-time paid summer internships. UICA encourages students from all backgrounds to explore careers in nonprofit settings, promote engagement with the University of Iowa, support and advance the university and its programs through meaningful pre-professional opportunities, and support potential graduates to obtain roles within our organization.

  • Participate in stewardship strategy meetings with stewardship liaisons and development officers to learn how stewardship supports donor engagement and long-term philanthropic relationships.

  • Utilize the organization's fundraising CRM to document stewardship activities, track donor engagement, and support stewardship reporting efforts.

  • Collaborate with stewardship team members to develop, create, and distribute personalized ThankView messages to donors.

Qualifications

  • Must be within driving distance of our Iowa City, IA office.

title: Project Engineering Intern
description:
Internship Objective

Develop practical engineering skills through hands-on experience in a manufacturing environment by supporting capital, maintenance, and process improvement projects. The intern will gain exposure to engineering design, documentation, commissioning, and plant operations while building proficiency in AutoCAD, engineering drawings, data analysis, and process equipment fundamentals.

Working closely with operators, technicians, engineers, vendors, and leadership, the intern will apply engineering principles to solve real-world challenges, improve equipment reliability and operational performance, and lead at least one improvement initiative or workstream from concept through implementation. This role provides a balanced mix of office and plant-floor experience, offering valuable exposure to industrial systems, project execution, and cross-functional collaboration.

What You'll Do

Project Support

  • Assist with scoping, planning, and executing engineering tasks within capital and continuous-improvement projects.
  • Support commissioning, equipment startups, trial runs, and data collection.
  • Participate in PSSR walk-throughs, design reviews, vendor meetings, and project standups.

Technical Documentation

  • Create and update SOPs, commissioning checklists, acceptance criteria, equipment lists, and technical reports.
  • Review and markup engineering drawings (AutoCAD, P&IDs, layouts, electrical schematics).
  • Maintain organized project files, trackers, and documentation libraries.

Plant-Floor Engagement

  • Observe equipment operation, verify field conditions, and gather feedback from operators and maintenance.
  • Support troubleshooting by documenting findings, capturing photos, and relaying information to engineers.
  • Follow PPE guidelines and comply with all EHS&S requirements.

Vendor & Contractor Coordination

  • Compare vendor quotes, collect specifications, and prepare technical summaries.
  • Document meetings, track action items, and support communication between engineering and external partners.
  • Assist with scheduling site visits and monitoring installation progress.

Data & Analysis

  • Collect and log process data during trials, startups, and testing.
  • Build and maintain Excel-based trackers for timelines, equipment lists, action items, and project metrics.
  • Support investigations by organizing data and observations.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Communicate with Engineering, Maintenance, Production, EHS&S, R&D, and contractors.
  • Provide clear, concise updates tailored to both technical and non-technical audiences, including Sr. Leadership.
  • Surface issues early and help maintain project momentum.

What You'll Bring

  • Currently enrolled in a bachelor's degree program in a relevant discipline at an accredited university, with an anticipated graduation date between December 2027 and May 2029 (rising junior or rising senior).
  • Strong academic performance with a minimum GPA of 3.0.
  • Available to work full-time for 12 weeks during summer 2027.
  • Reliable transportation to and from the work location.
  • Authorization to work in the United States.

Preferred Skills

  • Pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field.
  • Strong communication skills: able to interact professionally with plant operators through Sr. Leadership.
  • Ability to work 50% at a desk and 50% on the plant floor.
  • Basic proficiency in AutoCAD or similar CAD software.
  • Strong Excel skills (formulas, lookups, pivot tables preferred).
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and equipment manuals.
  • Solid technical writing skills for SOPs and documentation.
  • Curiosity, attention to detail, and willingness to learn industrial systems.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.

What You'll Receive

As of the date of this posting, a good faith estimate of the current pay scale for this position is $20 to $25 per hour. Placement in the range depends on several factors such as experience, skills, geography and may change over time.

title: Part-Time Online Course Facilitator:  AI/ML Technology and Architecture
description:
Department Summary

eCornell delivers expertly crafted online certificate programs designed by Cornell University faculty. Our facilitators play a central role in creating dynamic, engaging, and highly interactive learning experiences. We are committed to providing an exceptional student experience through live interactions, meaningful feedback, and authentic engagement.


The Opportunity

We are seeking experienced professionals to join our team as Course Facilitators in our AI/ML Technology and Architecture portfolio. Facilitators are not course authors or adjunct faculty but are vital to ensuring the effective delivery of content created by Cornell faculty.


In this role, you will complement our asynchronous course content by:

  • Leading engaging live sessions that engage students in discussion of machine learning, natural language processing, large language models (LLMs), and the design of AI-powered applications and agents.
  • Providing personalized and constructive feedback (written and recorded video) on discussion boards, assignments, Python coding projects in Jupyter notebooks, and written analyses, such as model training and evaluation, text-analysis pipelines, LLM fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, AI agents, and AI opportunity and governance assessments.
  • Coaching learners to troubleshoot their code and connect AI/ML techniques, architectural trade-offs, and responsible AI practices to real-world business and technical settings.
  • Fostering meaningful connections with students in a highly interactive online environment.

To be considered for this position, please include a cover letter with your application materials.

Cover letter instructions [IMPORTANT]

As part of the Course Facilitator position at eCornell, video interaction with students is a key component of the role. Facilitators are expected to engage with students through live video sessions and in response to project submissions. Video interactions allow facilitators to better engage with students, provide real-time feedback, and create an inclusive and personable learning experience.

As such, we encourage applicants to submit a video response to the question below using Loom. While submitting the video is optional, it is highly encouraged.

  • Answer the following question in a short video (3 minutes max):

What excites you most about facilitating at eCornell, and how would you bring that enthusiasm into your interactions with students?

  • Record your response using Loom (free service).
  • Copy and paste the video link into your cover letter.

Program-Specific Focus


Facilitators will support AI/ML Technology and Architecture certificate programs, which help working professionals move from using AI to building with it through hands-on Python work.


The ideal candidate has 8+ years of professional experience in one or more of the following areas, with the ability to explain these concepts to working professionals:


  • Applied machine learning, from data preparation and feature engineering through training, evaluating, and improving common models such as regression, decision trees, and ensembles.
  • Natural language processing, including text preprocessing, vectorization and embeddings, document classification, topic modeling, clustering, and sentiment analysis.
  • How large language models work, including tokenization, embeddings, attention and transformer architectures, and fine-tuning.
  • Building LLM-powered applications, including prompt and context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and AI agents.
  • AI strategy, governance, and ethics, including evaluating AI opportunities, human oversight, AI security, and bias and fairness.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Engage Students: Lead dynamic live discussions that foster interaction and deepen understanding.
  • Provide Feedback: Deliver clear, constructive, and authentic feedback on student submissions, including recorded video responses.
  • Facilitate Effectively: Manage online discussions, respond promptly to student inquiries, and track student progress.
  • Commitment: Facilitate a minimum of 1-2 courses per month with consistent engagement and preparation.
  • Onboarding and Training: Complete an in-depth onboarding program, including shadowing live courses, participating in debrief sessions, and mastering the assigned certificate program.
  • Continuous Improvement: Engage in ongoing training and professional development to stay current with emerging learning methodologies, educational technologies, and best practices in online facilitation.

Required Qualifications:

  • Has 8+ years of relevant professional experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Graduate degree in computer science, data science, statistics, information science, or a related field preferred.
  • Brings substantial professional experience as a data scientist, machine learning engineer, NLP engineer, AI engineer, or AI/software architect, with a track record of building and deploying ML or AI solutions that deliver business value.
  • Is proficient in Python and can quickly read, debug, and evaluate students’ code in Jupyter notebooks.
  • Has hands-on experience with the tools used in the program, such as NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, NLTK or spaCy, Hugging Face Transformers or PyTorch, commercial LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini), and frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or the OpenAI Agents SDK.
  • Can explain the math (probability and statistics, linear algebra, and gradient-based optimization) underlying ML models.
  • Communicates complex technical concepts clearly to professionals with varied technical backgrounds and uses relevant industry examples to help learners apply course concepts.
  • Is comfortable facilitating live online discussions, providing timely and impactful feedback to busy professionals.
  • Possesses exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal.
  • Is comfortable with technology for instruction
  • Loom video submission with application

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Brings 15+ years of progressive experience in data science, machine learning, NLP, AI engineering, or software and solutions architecture.
  • Has held senior technical, architectural, or leadership roles in which they designed, deployed, or scaled ML, NLP, or generative AI systems in production, including making architecture, model selection, and build vs. buy decisions.
  • Has hands-on experience fine-tuning LLMs (e.g., LoRA, DPO), working with open models from the Hugging Face Hub, building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, or developing autonomous and multi-agent systems.
  • Has experience with SQL and relational databases, and with deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow/Keras or PyTorch.
  • Has led cross-functional teams and can share firsthand experience with AI opportunity assessment, AI governance and risk management, model evaluation in production, and the trade-offs involved in bringing AI solutions from prototype to deployment.
  • Experience teaching, coaching, or mentoring technical professionals.

**Sponsorship for employment visa is not available for this position**


What We Offer:

  • Comprehensive onboarding and training program to set you up for success.
  • Access to ongoing professional development resources and periodic training updates.
  • Opportunities to contribute to an exceptional online student experience.
  • A collaborative and supportive facilitator community.

Additional Information

  • This position is based in Ithaca, New York, however, the successful applicant may perform this role remotely anywhere within the United States.
  • The New York Convenience of employer guidelines require New York State individual tax reporting and withholdings for this position. Additional individual state income tax filings may also be required if working temporarily outside New York State.

Important Notes

  • eCornell will not store or download your video; it remains on your personal Loom account.
  • Video submissions are assessed solely based on communication, clarity, and engagement—not on personal characteristics unrelated to job performance.

We look forward to learning more about you!

  • Location: These positions are remote and open to candidates located anywhere within the U.S.
  • Employment Type: Casual, non-benefits-eligible positions.
  • Restrictions: No visa sponsorship or relocation assistance is available for these positions.

Join Us

If you’re an experienced semiconductor manufacturer and are passionate about helping professionals learn the theory and practices critical to the process, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and become an integral part of the Cornell team!

title: Summer Associate (1L)
description:
Our Toledo, Ohio office is now accepting 1L applications for our 2027 Summer Associate Program! Please be sure to upload your resume, transcript and writing sample for consideration.

Applications must be submitted on the Shumaker website by January 17, 2027 for consideration. If you have any questions or need to provide updated documents, please contact us at recruiting@shumaker.com.

We look upon our summer associate program as the major source of our future associates and partners. Shumaker recruits summer associates after their first and second years in leading law schools nationwide, and we accept you for inclusion because we see you as a “Shumaker lawyer.” Your learning experience shows you exactly what to expect at Shumaker if you practice law with us, as you will have the opportunity to work on a wide variety of projects involving multiple practice areas. You’ll attend court appearances, discovery proceedings, client meetings and transaction closings. You’ll draft legal documents that are filed with the court system or delivered directly to clients. In other words, you’ll find out very quickly what it’s like to practice law!

Why You Benefit

Wherever possible you’ll have the opportunity to attend client meetings, closings, negotiations, depositions, trials and courtroom hearings. The lawyers you work with will also ask you to draft research memoranda, litigation pleadings, motions and briefs, and a variety of transactional documents. It’s a well-rounded approach that lets you demonstrate your analytical, advocacy and writing skills, and that is as close to a first-year associate’s experience as can be made.

It’s a realistic approach that you don’t get at school – or at other firms, where summer associates are rotated through to multiple practice groups. Doing multiple projects for multiple people is not only more realistic, it gives you the opportunity to learn more about your own optimal skill set. That’s to your advantage, and ours.

You’ll definitely have an enjoyable time, but with a purpose: getting to know your peers and the other lawyers we hope to have you work with in a year or two. We encourage you to participate in events like dinners, sporting events and practice group get-togethers. Much of what we have planned will allow you to experience the city where you chose to spend the summer.

What You Can Expect from Shumaker

Your summer experience begins with our recruiting process, which we’re proud to say we never suspended during the recession. We focus on schools that are leaders in our geographical areas: for example, The University of Michigan, Notre Dame and The Ohio State University in the Midwest, and The University of Florida, Florida State University and Stetson University for our Tampa and Sarasota offices.

But we also cover major national schools like Emory University and Georgetown University. You’ll meet with one or two Shumaker lawyers for virtual or on-campus interviews, then receive a callback for further interviews with partners and associates at each office based on what we’ve learned from you as well as our assignment needs by office.

Once you begin in the program your summer coordinator will oversee your workload and make sure you have the projects that match your interests. You’ll not only be invited to attend regular practice group meetings where legal training is provided, you’ll also attend formal in-house seminars on topics like bankruptcy, trusts and estates, employee benefits and mergers and acquisitions. It’s all part of an experience specially designed to help summer associates develop the key professional skills and legal insight unique to their practice area.

As you continue to work on projects, you will be evaluated throughout the summer on each project you do. Lawyers who assign projects to you are required to provide substantive feedback in connection with each project, and if we feel you need improvement we bring it up at once in a way designed to help you. Additional mid-summer and final evaluations let you know where you stand, and we review all of these evaluations in making our offer decisions.

Physical Requirements

This job may require frequent sitting and standing, with occasional walking, bending, and lifting. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities to ensure equal access to employment opportunities. If you require accommodations during the application or interview process, please let us know.

title: Transmission Project Developer
description:
Transmission Project Developer

Location Fergus Falls, MN

Grade 11

Otter Tail Power Company is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Transmission Project Developer to support the development and execution of transmission line projects. This role plays a critical part in advancing infrastructure initiatives that support reliable electric service and regional growth.

This role reports to Supervisor Transmission Project Development.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the development of transmission line projects from concept through execution.
  • Obtain major permits required for the construction of transmission lines, ensuring compliance with all regulatory requirements.
  • Manage permitting timelines and coordinate with federal, state, and local agencies.
  • Facilitate community engagement efforts, including outreach, communication, and relationship management with stakeholders.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including engineering, environmental, legal, and asset management.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience in project development, permitting, or infrastructure projects (utility or transmission experience preferred).
  • Strong knowledge of regulatory and permitting processes related to transmission or energy infrastructure.
  • Proven ability to manage complex projects with multiple stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including experience with public outreach and stakeholder engagement.
  • Strong organizational and contract management capabilities.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

What We Offer

    • Retirement Savings Fund with employer match

To apply, visit our careers page at . Applications accepted through November 20, 2026.

This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship at this time.

title: Revenue Manager
description:
Job Summary

The Revenue Manager is responsible for implementing hotel revenue management objectives across their managed portfolio, which encompasses maximizing revenues and profit through rate and inventory management of all market segments at the hotel. The Revenue Manager will take an active role in the hotel's pricing and distribution of inventory across various channels of distribution to maximize revenues, working closely with their Regional VP/Regional Director. The position supports their portfolio in meetings, analyzing trends in the group and transient segments, exceeding budgeted goals and setting group ceilings, target rates in conjunction with the sales team.

Essential functions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

  • Develop, implement, monitor and control rate strategies
  • Develop action plans to counteract market changes
  • Update and change restrictions and inventory allotments
  • Maximize RevPAR by analyzing past trends and future demand forecast to set/adjust sales strategies designed to increase market share, RevPAR growth and optimize the market mix
  • Generate daily, weekly, monthly revenue management reports
  • Facilitate weekly revenue strategy meetings for assigned portfolio.
  • Analyze and optimize distribution channels for the maximum benefit of penetration
  • Contribute to website content and maintenance of website content
  • Manage property participation and production through 3rd Party Internet sites and other distribution channels
  • Monitor all distribution channels to ensure content accuracy, rate parity, and pricing integrity
  • Develop relationships with vendors and Internet wholesalers to accomplish revenue goals and negotiate placement for hotels
  • Work closely with the sales and e-commerce department to create eNewsletters, hotel packages, and other marketing-related efforts
  • Manage and maintain group and transient inventory controls
  • Provide critical analysis of strategies, room's statistics and demand factor
  • Develop short and long-term top-line rooms revenue hotel forecasts upon request from the Regional VP/Regional Director and VP of Revenue Management.
  • Participate and prepare rolling forecast and annual budget for each property
  • Loads all preferred, consortia and promotional rates in GDS and PMS
  • Ensure that all rooms statistics reports, including the financial statement, and any other related reports are accurate and consistent
  • Ensure that all revenue management related systems are maintained
  • Understand the reservations process including the distribution channels and reservations flow
  • Attend Weekly Sales Meeting to maintain communication of strategies and need periods
  • Champion the Revenue Management culture to property level personnel
  • Active involvement with General Managers' engagement
  • Demonstrate the ability to relate to, communicate with, and motivate associates to sustain high performance and quality levels

Competencies

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
  • Strong Microsoft Office skills, specifically Excel
  • Demonstrate the ability to lead by example
  • Ability to work well under pressure
  • Passion for excellence and exceeding expectations
  • Self-motivated, and ability to work with little to no supervision
  • Hilton, Marriott and IHG experience preferred

Physical demands

  • Long hours sometimes required.
  • Medium work-exerting up to 30 pounds of force occasionally, and/or 20 pounds of force to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects.
  • Ability to sit for long periods at a time.

Travel required

  • 5-10%

Required education and experience

  • Four-year degree or equivalent experience
  • Two years of regional revenue management experience - including Marriott, Hilton and IHG Brands
  • Excellent communication skills including presenting data trends and strategic planning.
