title: Core Trainer, China Grove - Full Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Summary

The Core Trainer will assist with the on-boarding and job task-based training of Seasonal and Core Colleagues. The trainer should demonstrate knowledge of all job tasks within their assigned department and function and deliver a high-level of accuracy and consistency when performing the work, training colleagues, or reviewing completed work. Core Trainers will be crossed-trained in all areas of the facility. This role plays a critical part in developing colleagues through training, retraining and supporting both new and current team members to ensure operational excellence, accuracy and consistency. The Core Trainer demonstrates a deep understanding of the end- to- end supply chain flow and embodies the genuine hospitality and inclusive culture of Macy’s.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

What You Will Do

Training Support

  • Support Core and Seasonal Colleagues in assigned departments/functions by training and coaching on essential job tasks to ensure successful job performance.
  • Provide onboarding and operational training for new hires to ensure understanding of operating procedures, safety expectations, quality standards, and productivity goals.
  • Provide refresher training and retraining for existing colleagues who are not meeting operational performance, quality, safety, or productivity standards to reinforce proper operating procedures and improve overall performance.
  • Ensure work instructions, safety guidelines, and quality expectations are consistently followed throughout daily operations.
  • Consult and partner with designated Training Ambassador regarding work instructions, process updates, operational gaps, and training opportunities to ensure consistency and standardization across the facility.
  • Serve as a cross-functional trainer capable of supporting operational training needs across multiple departments throughout the facility.
  • Complete training checklists and conduct follow-up to ensure colleagues successfully complete the training period and achieve operational standards.
  • Perform frequent quality and productivity audits of work processed and provide immediate coaching and corrective feedback when needed.
  • Observe workflows, minimize errors, assess job proficiency, and retrain colleagues as necessary to improve performance and productivity.
  • Partner with Warehouse Managers and Leads to identify operational gaps, problem solve performance issues and implement training solutions that improve execution and productivity.
  • Demonstrate a passion for training and developing others while creating an engaging learning environment that motivates colleagues to succeed.
  • Adapt training methods to support different learning styles and operational demands.

Communication

  • Greet colleagues on their first day of employment and conduct orientation activities including building tours, time clock procedures, and reliability expectations.
  • Act as a point person for colleagues by answering questions related to processes, functions, safety, and operational expectations.
  • Communicate issues, concerns, and performance trends promptly to Managers, or Shift/Functional Directors for quick resolution.
  • Build positive working relationships and effectively influence and motivate others to drive accountability, engagement, and productivity.
  • Maintain strong attention to detail when documenting training progress, identifying performance trends, and communicating operational updates.

Safety Throughout Shift Safety Advocate

  • Demonstrate and reinforce safe workplace behaviors consistent with company safety policies and procedures.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Maintain regular, dependable attendance and punctuality.
  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships and ensures authentic connections with colleagues, customers, and communities.
  • Demonstrate flexibility to support changing business needs, peak operations, and cross-functional training initiatives.

Who You Are

Must be able to:

  • Strong attention to detail is essential to maintain quality, safety, and operational efficiency.
  • Understand and communicate effectively with, co-workers, leads, and facility leadership.
  • Read and understand employment policies and safety rules/procedures in English.
  • Demonstrate an affinity and passion for training, coaching, and developing others.
  • Exhibit strong attention to detail and the ability to consistently reinforce standard operating procedures.
  • Motivate, influence, and engage colleagues to achieve operational productivity and quality goals.
  • Partner effectively with Warehouse Managers, Training Ambassadors and Leads to resolve operational challenges and improve team performance.
  • Demonstrate strong interpersonal, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Positively impact team success in a fast-paced environment.
  • Manage multiple priorities and processes effectively while maintaining operational standards.
  • Work assigned scheduled including days, evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.

Essential Physical Requirements You Will Perform

  • This position requires lifting, constant moving, standing, and reaching with arms and hands.
  • Involves standing for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 50lbs., stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders.
  • Reaching, including above eye level, crouching, kneeling, and stooping.
  • Involves close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment.
  • Frequent use of computers and other technology, necessary to perform job functions, including handheld equipment.

Supply Chain Only and Colleagues Working in a Supply Chain Facility except in locations governed by a Collective Bargaining Agreement:

Random drug testing for all colleagues will be conducted on a monthly or semi-monthly basis, depending upon factors including but not limited to the size of the facility and the number of colleagues on roll. Colleagues will be randomly selected for testing by a third party. Testing must be completed on the same workday the colleague is informed of selection for testing, absent extenuating circumstances. In all circumstances, testing must be completed within 24 hours of notification.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!

Medical Advisor (Part-Time, 2 days/week, 1-year term)

CPSO Medical Advisors support to advance and improve patient care by applying their clinical knowledge and skills, expertise in leadership, collaborative team functioning, education and mentoring, and high standards of professionalism. This expertise is applied to specific cases involving physicians undergoing investigations, assessments, and application for independent practice certificates. Medical Advisors also use their specialized knowledge on assignments and projects designed to build and maintain public trust in the medical profession.

Specifically, CPSO Medical Advisors:

  • Liaise with other bodies as required such as RCPSC, CFPC, OMA, PHP, CMPA.

  • Have a broad understanding of medicine in general through clinical practice, teaching or leadership of medical programs.
  • Demonstrated professionalism and collaboration skills.

title: Advancement Summer Internship Program - Legal Intern
company: University of Iowa Center for Advancement
description:
The University of Iowa Center for Advancement (UICA) is currently providing opportunities for full-time paid summer internships. UICA encourages students from all backgrounds to explore careers in nonprofit settings, promote engagement with the University of Iowa, support and advance the university and its programs through meaningful pre-professional opportunities, and support potential graduates to obtain roles within our organization.

The UICA will provide 9 intern opportunities that provide 10 weeks of work experience, June 1 - August 6. Interns will earn $18/hour and will be provided with the flexibility and technology to work from home two days per week if desired. Up to five unpaid vacation days will be available throughout the internship program if desired. At the conclusion of the internship, all interns are expected to give a final presentation highlighting their experience and projects they have worked on. Housing and benefits are not available as part of the intern experience and interns must be within driving distance of our Iowa City, IA office.

As the Legal Intern, you will support the University of Iowa Center for Advancement's legal department by contributing to a variety of legal, compliance, governance, and operational initiatives. Your work will help advance important projects that support the organization's mission while providing additional capacity for legal research, policy review, contract support, and compliance-related work. This internship will provide hands-on experience across a broad range of legal issues affecting nonprofit organizations, exposure to the practice of in-house counsel, and opportunities to learn how legal guidance supports fundraising, engagement, and mission-driven decision-making. Through meaningful projects and mentorship from experienced professionals, you will gain valuable insight into nonprofit law and the role of legal counsel within a complex organization.

Core Responsibilities

  • Research topics related to nonprofit law, tax-exempt organizations, charitable giving, governance, privacy, and regulatory compliance and assist with related projects.
  • Assist with reviewing, analyzing, and summarizing contracts, policies, regulations, and legal guidance.
  • Assist with special projects designed to improve the legal department's efficiency, organization, and service to internal clients.
  • Participate in meetings with attorneys and organizational partners to observe how legal advice informs business and mission-based decisions.
  • Perform other legal and administrative duties under attorney supervision.

Qualifications

  • Completion of at least one year of law school by the start of the internship.
  • Open to students entering their second year of college in Fall 2027 through students graduating from any college or university in 2027
  • Must be within driving distance of our Iowa City, IA office.

title: Salgsmedarbejder til Køkkentilbehør, 30 timer pr. uge, Taastrup
description:
Derfor er vi helt vilde med dig

Trives du med rådgivende salg og lagerarbejde, hvor man sjældent står stille og aldrig keder sig? Så er det måske dig vi leder efter!

Vi lægger desuden vægt på at du:
• Er serviceorienteret, er fyldt med energi og kan lide at bruge din krop
• Er selvstændig og tager ansvar for at prioritere dine arbejdsopgaver, så tiden udnyttes mest effektivt
• Elsker at holde orden og sørge for at alt er pænt og ryddeligt og du ikke er bange for at skulle rykke rundt på en masse varer
• Taler og forstår dansk.

En dag I dit liv hos os

Denne stilling er i afdelingen for Køkkentilbehør og er placeret på 1. sal i varehuset.
Salgsafdelingerne på 1. sal, hvor der sælges boligtilbehør, arbejder ofte sammen og hjælper hinanden i hverdagen. Du kommer derfor også til at opleve, og blive oplært i, de andre afdelinger på 1. sal.

Din hverdag vil bl.a. bestå af:
• At rådgive og inspirere vores kunder ud fra deres behov og ønsker
• Håndtering af varer og klargøring af salgspladser og udstillinger, så varerne er tilgængelige for kunderne - Vi har varer og udstillinger, fra gulv til loft, så noget af arbejdet vil foregå på stige
• Oprydning, så udstillinger og afdelingen altid er præsentable og inspirerende
• At gøre klar til de produkter, der kommer næste dag, ved at at tage pap og rykke produkter rundt
• Ved behov; hjælpe i andre salgsafdelinger, som f.eks Textil, Bad, Planter osv.

Vores team i IKEA

Du bliver en del af et team af både fuldtids- og deltidsmedarbejdere i et stort varehus. Vi arbejder tæt sammen med andre afdelinger, og du får derfor erfaring med at samarbejde med mange forskellige mennesker. Vi har et rigtig godt sammenhold, hvor vi bakker hinanden op og løfter i flok. Der er derfor plads til at være lige præcis den, du er, og du har mulighed for at skabe et stærkt socialt netværk. Vi sørger for den rette oplæring, så du kan føle dig tryg og kompetent i jobbet.

Har du spørgsmål eller brug for hjælp? Lad os tale med hinanden!

Du er velkommen til at kontakte Shopkeeper Nilas Barfoed på nilas.barfoed@ingka.ikea.com ved spørgsmål til stillingen. Vi gør opmærksom på, at vi udelukkende modtager ansøgninger via vores rekrutteringssystem og ikke via e-mail.

Yderligere informationer

• Stillingen er på 30 timer pr. uge i gennemsnit
• Din arbejdstid placeres primært i varehusets åbningstider, og du skal forvente at have 2 aftenvagter pr. uge. Vi arbejder hver 2. weekend, både lørdag og søndag
• Løn efter HK’s butiksoverenskomst, herunder pension- og fritvalgsordning samt forskudttidstillæg
• Vi har forskellige personalegoder, herunder privat sundhedsforsikring, massage, kantine, personalerabat, rabatklub med eksterne samarbejdspartnere, årsgave mm.
• Der kan i ansættelsesprocessen blive stillet krav om fremvisning af straffeattest
• Ønsket opstart pr. 1. januar 2027 eller efter aftale
• Søg senest d. 18. november 2026
• OBS: Vi indkalder løbende til samtaler og forbeholder os retten til at lukke jobopslaget, når vi har modtaget tilstrækkeligt med relevante kandidater.

Hos IKEA tror vi på mennesker – ikke perfekte CV’er. Det vigtigste er din energi og lyst til at gøre en forskel. Søg nu – uanset om du er ung, senior eller midt i mellem!

Applications must be submitted on the Shumaker website by January 17, 2027 for consideration. If you have any questions or need to provide updated documents, please email the updated documents to recruiting@shumaker.com.

We look upon our summer associate program as the major source of our future associates and partners. Shumaker recruits summer associates after their first and second years in leading law schools nationwide, and we accept you for inclusion because we see you as a “Shumaker lawyer.” Your learning experience shows you exactly what to expect at Shumaker if you practice law with us, as you will have the opportunity to work on a wide variety of projects involving multiple practice areas. You’ll attend court appearances, discovery proceedings, client meetings and transaction closings. You’ll draft legal documents that are filed with the court system or delivered directly to clients. Why You Benefit

Wherever possible you’ll have the opportunity to attend client meetings, closings, negotiations, depositions, trials and courtroom hearings. The lawyers you work with will also ask you to draft research memoranda, litigation pleadings, motions and briefs, and a variety of transactional documents. It’s a well-rounded approach that lets you demonstrate your analytical, advocacy and writing skills, and that is as close to a first-year associate’s experience as can be made.

It’s a realistic approach that you don’t get at school – or at other firms, where summer associates are rotated through to multiple practice groups. Doing multiple projects for multiple people is not only more realistic, it gives you the opportunity to learn more about your own optimal skill set. That’s to your advantage, and ours.

You’ll definitely have an enjoyable time, but with a purpose: getting to know your peers and the other lawyers we hope to have you work with in a year or two. We encourage you to participate in events like dinners, sporting events and practice group get-togethers. Much of what we have planned will allow you to experience the city where you chose to spend the summer.

What You Can Expect from Shumaker

Your summer experience begins with our recruiting process, which we’re proud to say we never suspended during the recession. We focus on schools that are leaders in our geographical areas: for example, The University of Michigan, Notre Dame and The Ohio State University in the Midwest, and The University of Florida, Florida State University and Stetson University for our Tampa and Sarasota offices.

But we also cover major national schools like Emory University and Georgetown University. You’ll meet with one or two Shumaker lawyers for virtual or on-campus interviews, then receive a callback for further interviews with partners and associates at each office based on what we’ve learned from you as well as our assignment needs by office.

Once you begin in the program your summer coordinator will oversee your workload and make sure you have the projects that match your interests. You’ll not only be invited to attend regular practice group meetings where legal training is provided, you’ll also attend formal in-house seminars on topics like bankruptcy, trusts and estates, employee benefits and mergers and acquisitions. It’s all part of an experience specially designed to help summer associates develop the key professional skills and legal insight unique to their practice area.

As you continue to work on projects, you will be evaluated throughout the summer on each project you do. Lawyers who assign projects to you are required to provide substantive feedback in connection with each project, and if we feel you need improvement we bring it up at once in a way designed to help you. Additional mid-summer and final evaluations let you know where you stand, and we review all of these evaluations in making our offer decisions.

Physical Requirements

This job may require frequent sitting and standing, with occasional walking, bending, and lifting. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities to ensure equal access to employment opportunities. If you require accommodations during the application or interview process, please let us know.

title: SA23M5 Sr. Director, Commercial Operations
description:
CAS uses intuitive technology, unparalleled scientific content, and unmatched human expertise to help companies create groundbreaking innovations that benefit the world. As the scientific information solutions division of the American Chemical Society, CAS manages the largest curated reservoir of scientific knowledge and, for 119 years, has helped innovators mine, assess, and apply that information to keep businesses thriving. The CAS team is global, diverse, and endlessly curious, and it strives to make scientific insights accessible to innovators worldwide.

CAS is currently seeking a Sr. Director, Commercial Operations on our Sales team. This position is located at our headquarters in Columbus, Ohio.

Position Summary

The Sr. Director, Commercial Operations leads the operational backbone of the commercial organization: GTM and market planning, pricing and renewals, customer agreements, sales analysis and territory design, customer operations, and the technology and data foundation that supports all of it. This role consolidates what is today split across four largely vacant leadership seats, and reports directly to the Chief Customer Officer / SVP, Sales & Customer Experience.

This role carries roughly three to six direct reports, several of whose seats are currently open, and about fifteen to twenty indirect reports across the workstreams it leads. It carries budget responsibility and is classified as exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act.

This is not a pure operations or analytics role. The function's most immediate mandate is forecasting: building a rigorous, defensible revenue and pipeline forecasting process that the executive team can rely on, and that does not exist in a consistent form today. Because forecast credibility depends on field credibility, this role requires someone who has carried a quota and led a sales team before, not only someone who has analyzed one.

This is also a developmental seat. The Sr. Director is expected to build direct working relationships with the three regional sales leaders, with Commercial Enablement, Marketing and Product Management, and to demonstrate the commercial judgment and cross-functional leadership associated with broader general management.

The function this role leads has become process-heavy without becoming faster or easier to work with. A core mandate of this role is to lean out that accumulated process debt: aggressively reduce cycle time and friction in how the commercial engine runs, and materially cut the administrative burden Commercial Operations places on sales representatives, so sellers spend their time on customers and outcomes rather than navigating internal process. This supports a broader shift already underway in how sales talent is hired and developed, away from process-heavy profiles and toward ones focused on customer outcomes. This mandate is as central to the role as forecasting rigor; a candidate who can only deliver one is not the right fit.

Position Responsibilities

Commercial Forecasting & Revenue Rigor

  • Own the end-to-end revenue and pipeline forecasting process across new business, renewals, and pricing, in direct partnership with Finance
  • Invigorate forecast methodology, cadence, confidence categories, and variance analysis as a standing discipline, not an ad hoc monthly exercise
  • Present forecast and pipeline health directly to the CCO and, on a recurring basis, to the broader executive team (CEO, CFO, etc.)

    Process Simplification & Seller Friction Reduction

    • Lead an aggressive simplification agenda across GTM & Market Planning, Pricing & Renewals, Customer Agreements and CAM, Sales Analysis & Planning, Customer Operations & ID Management, Technology and Commercial Data: measured by cycle-time reduction and process elimination, not by process maturity or added structure
    • Partner with Technology & Business Data to identify and deploy AI and agentic automation, starting with high-manual-volume functions such as the Customer Center's fully live-agent call handling today
    • Create targeted approach for reducing non-selling hours per rep per week through process simplification and leaning
    • Actively retire or consolidate legacy processes and reporting requirements that persist for historical reasons rather than active business need

        Commercial Operations Leadership

        • GTM & Market Planning: own launch cadence, stage-gate governance, and market/ICP validation, absorbed from the former GTM Coordinator role
        • Pricing & Renewals: own the platform for new business, renewals, and order entry; own bundling strategy; and own the Small Accounts Team, an inbound-only function handling new-logo intake and renewals for accounts at or below $50K ACV across North America and EMEA
        • Customer Agreement & CAM: own Customer Agreement end to end, including the order-to-cash portion
        • Sales Analysis & Planning: own territory design, sales reporting and collaborate with HR & Finance on incentive compensation
        • Customer Operations & ID Management: own the customer support platform, identity management, and service-level standards, including modernizing a support model that today handles all inbound calls manually, with no automated or agentic support in place
        • Technology & Data Foundation: own the shared tech/data backbone, the AI and tools roadmap, legacy system migration, Salesforce.com administration, and translation of business requirements into system changes

                Cross-Functional Partnership

                • Partner with Commercial Enablement on the launch stage-gate process, including AI-fluency readiness as a go/no-go criterion
                • Serve as the data and cadence partner to Strategic Accounts on Top 150 health-score reporting, on a defined refresh schedule
                • Maintain a direct escalation channel into Services and CSS leadership for delivery-caused account risk, distinct from the executive review cycle

                  Sales Leadership & Field Credibility

                  • Bring firsthand sales leadership experience to territory design, incentive structure, and forecast discipline; sellers need to trust this function, not merely comply with it
                  • Partner directly and credibly with the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regional leaders as a peer with sales-floor experience, not solely as a systems and process owner

                  Team Leadership & Talent

                  • Lead a distributed organization of roughly six workstream leads and their teams; fill and develop the leadership structure/seats that are needed in Commercial Operations
                  • Make speed, simplification, and reduced friction the operating discipline for a function that has run process-heavy; more standardization is not the goal, less friction is
                  • Partner with internal staff to build out the Small Accounts Team from the ground up (Renewals and In-bound BD), including its first hires, a new, inbound-only function not yet staffed

                        Background Experience

                        Suitable candidate background includes:

                        • 10+ years in commercial or go-to-market roles, including a minimum of 3–5 years in direct sales leadership (managing quota-carrying representatives or front-line sales managers) — required, not preferred
                        • Demonstrated ownership of revenue or pipeline forecasting at scale, with a track record of improving forecast accuracy over time
                        • Experience with CRM platform oversight (Salesforce.com preferred) and sales compensation design, while working cross-functionally with Finance, HR, and GTM/product-launch processes

The University of Iowa Center for Advancement (UICA) is currently providing opportunities for full- time paid summer internships. Develop a best practices resource focused on volunteer recruitment, engagement, recognition, stewardship, and management.
  • Assist in developing volunteer resources, toolkits, and engagement materials designed to enhance the volunteer experience. Collaborate with Alumni Engagement staff to create strategies that strengthen volunteer retention, satisfaction, and continued involvement with the university.
  • Participate in team meetings and planning discussions to gain exposure to alumni and volunteer engagement strategies, stewardship practices, and advancement operations.

Qualifications

  • Open to students entering their second year of college in Fall 2027 through students graduating from any college or university in 2027
  • Must be within driving distance of our Iowa City, IA office.

title: Beauty Counter Manager - Kiko Milano, Temecula Promenade - Full Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As a Counter Manager, you will lead a dynamic team of Beauty Advisors while managing all aspects of a specific cosmetics brand. Your role blends leadership, creativity, and customer engagement—delivering genuine hospitality through personalized consultations, expert product application, and a deep understanding of each customer’s beauty and style preferences.

You’ll inspire teamwork to drive sales and elevate the customer experience by creating meaningful, long-lasting connections. With a strong focus on client development, you will cultivate a loyal customer base through outreach, follow-up, and consistent, personalized service.

In addition to meeting and exceeding sales goals, you’ll analyze business performance, execute vendor events and promotions, and partner with vendors and store leadership to grow the business. You'll also oversee stock presentation, hygiene standards, and team performance to ensure an exceptional and polished brand experience.

How Our Counter Managers Spend Their Day…

  • Every day starts with a positive example. As a Counter Manager, you come in energized and ready to inspire your team - wearing your name badge with pride, greeting colleagues with genuine warmth, and ensuring your counter is polished, organized, and fully prepared to welcome customers. You set the tone by reviewing daily sales goals, staying informed on new launches, top-performing products, and current beauty trends - so you're equipped to lead with confidence, support your team, and deliver exceptional service to every customer.
  • On the floor, you lead through action - welcoming customers with genuine hospitality, making eye contact, and starting friendly, personal conversations that build lasting relationships.
  • You help maintain a shoppable space by ensuring testers are clean and well-stocked, signage and pricing are current, and displays reflect brand standards. You lead by example, jumping in to support merchandising updates and keeping the space visually appealing and welcoming throughout the day.
  • You help the team Finish Strong - by coaching them to share Loyalty benefits, making sure customers leave with everything they need, and ending each interaction with a sincere thank-you, often using the customer’s name and adding a personal touch.
  • You know that service starts with each other. You model collaboration, honesty, and care - supporting your peers so the whole team can better serve our customers and communities.
  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

Who You Are and What You Will Do

  • Deliver exceptional customer service through personalized consultations and expert product knowledge
  • Build lasting relationships with clients and drive client development through outreach and follow-up
  • Review and analyze business performance of daily, weekly, monthly, seasonal, and annual sales results and implement strategies to grow business and improve results
  • Plan and execute in-store and vendor-led events to drive traffic and engagement
  • Maintain brand standards through proper merchandising, hygiene, and stock replenishment
  • Responsible for acquiring new customers by opening credit accounts and sharing loyalty benefits
  • Collaborate with vendors, personal stylists, and store leadership to optimize outcomes
  • Resolve customer concerns in a professional and customer-first manner
  • Stay informed on new launches, best-sellers, and beauty trends to support team education
  • Manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment with strong attention to detail
  • Demonstrate flexibility, sound judgment, and a passion for the beauty industry
  • 3–5 years of relevant retail, beauty, or leadership experience preferred
  • Flexible availability, including days, evenings, weekends and holidays with regular, dependable attendance and punctuality
  • Must be able to:
    • Understand and communicate effectively with customers, co-workers, and supervisors
    • Read and understand employment policies and safety rules/procedures in English

Essential Physical Requirements You Will Perform

  • This position requires talking, lifting, constant moving, standing, and reaching with arms and hands.
  • Standing for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 25lbs., stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders, reaching, including above eye level
  • Requires close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment
  • Frequent use of computers and other technology, necessary to perform job functions, including handheld equipment, cash register and ability to process register transactions

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

title: Account Representative (Downstream Chemicals)
description:
Account Representative (Downstream Chemicals)

Would you like to take ownership of our customers’ needs to help them operate safely and efficiently?

Do you enjoy providing a vital service to ensure successful on-site operations?

Join our Downstream Chemical Team

Our Downstream Chemical Team uses technology consisting of chemistry, knowledge expertise, Intellectual Property, correct application methods and monitoring to improve the water and process treatment applications at refinery and industrial plants while providing value to our clients.

Partner with the best

As an Account Representative, you will provide a vital service by implementing, monitoring, troubleshooting and evaluating chemical treatment programs. You will take ownership of a key customer account to ensure they have the services and products needed to operate safely and efficiently. You will become a trusted advisor to customers as you develop an understanding of our customer’s needs and operations.

Fueling your passion

As an Account Representative, you will be responsible for:

  • Overseeing the daily operation and performance of refinery process treatment programs to ensure exceptional service and value for customers.
  • Building and maintaining strong, trusted relationships with customers and cross-functional partners to drive collaboration and success.
  • Providing account management to understand customer needs, requirements and potential win-win sales opportunities.
  • Gathering, analyzing, and interpreting data to support troubleshooting efforts, service reporting, KPI reviews, customer meetings, and presentations.
  • Delivering field support, laboratory analysis, and technical expertise to assist customers with operational challenges, projects, turnarounds, shutdowns, and routine activities.
  • Monitoring and managing chemical inventory levels and coordinating product deliveries at customer location.
  • Supporting the safe loading and unloading of chemical tank trailers and totes as needed.

To be successful in this role you will have:

  • Have Bachelor’s Degree Preferred will take a High School Diploma.
  • Have 3 plus years' experience with refinery or industrial experience
  • Have Refinery or industrial operation experience with, process chemical additives, water treatment, finished fuels additives, refinery sales, process engineering, or engineering service experience
  • Have Solid understanding and knowledge of refinery process operation and utilities units
  • Have Understanding of industrial chemical treatment programs and sales process
  • Demonstrate mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills
  • Have experience working in a laboratory setting
  • Have comprehensive understanding of customer requirements and refinery market conditions
  • Display excellent verbal and written communications skills

Work in a way that works for you

We recognize that everyone is different and that the way in which people want to work and deliver at their best is different for everyone too. In this role, we can offer the following flexible working patterns:

This role is working with our customer on-site. When onsite, you will have the flexibility to work in line with customer working patterns.

Working with us

Our people are at the heart of what we do at Baker Hughes. We know we are stronger when our people are developed, engaged, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. We invest in wellbeing, capability development, and leadership growth across all levels.

Working for you

Our innovations have transformed the energy industry for over a century. To continue progressing, we look for individuals who embrace change and contribute to building the future.

What You Can Expect

  • Contemporary work-life balance policies and wellbeing activities
  • Comprehensive private medical care options
  • Safety net of life insurance and disability programs
  • Tailored financial programs
  • Education assistance
  • Generous parental leave
  • Mental health resources
  • Dependent care support
  • Additional elected or voluntary benefits

This position requires valid work authorization in the country of employment. The employer is unable to sponsor work authorization for this role at any time.

You will be eligible to participate in Company-sponsored benefit programs, including health & welfare programs and the Thrift Plan (401k). You will have a choice of coverage options that best suit your needs. Coverage options and contribution amounts are related to your benefit elections, base salary level, and specific requirements of each of these plans.

title: KM Legal Research Analyst
description:
As a member of the Knowledge Management & Innovation Department, the KM Research Analyst conducts sophisticated legal and non-legal research to respond to firm-wide reference and research requests from attorneys, administration and staff.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Monitors workflow; responds and completes department requests.
  • Provides comprehensive legal and business research using a variety of on-line and print resources, including proper use of AI tools.
  • Conducts complex substantive legal research, precedent document searching, expert witness research, legislative history research, judicial research, docket, and analytics searching.
  • Creates targeted, custom alerts to monitor developments in the law, docket tracks, and litigation searches.
  • Precisely, intelligently, and promptly communicates the results of research requests to the requestors.
  • Provides general support for KM research tools and resources (i.e. Westlaw Precision, Practical Law, and other related platforms).

ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Works on special projects (i.e., collection development) as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS (EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES):

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in related field required. Masters in Library & Information Science or Juris Doctor a plus.

Experience:

  • Minimum of three years of legal and business research experience in a legal, corporate or professional services environment.
  • Experience using AI tools a plus.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities:

  • Thorough and advanced knowledge of legal research and general business research
  • Knowledge of and ability to use on-line resources including AI functionality within tools. Resources include: Westlaw Precision/Practical Law with AI modules, Bloomberg Law, PACER, and other types of web-based services, including IP, corporate and securities research tools as well as the Microsoft suite of products.
  • Ability to synthesize relevant information needed for high-level decision making.
  • Excellent communication skills with particular emphasis on written communication
  • Ability to multitask, manage time, establish priorities, respond to emergencies and deal with individuals with patience and diplomacy.
  • Ability to maintain a service-oriented attitude, remaining poised under pressure.
  • Self-motivated, detail oriented and organized with the ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

This job operates in a clerical, office setting. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Sedentary work: Exertion of physical strength to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects up to 10 pounds. Work involves sitting most of the time. Walking and standing is often necessary in carrying out job duties.

title: Advancement Summer Internship Program - Alumni Engagement Intern
company: University of Iowa Center for Advancement
description:
The University of Iowa Center for Advancement (UICA) is currently providing opportunities for full- time paid summer internships. UICA encourages students from all backgrounds to explore careers in nonprofit settings, promote engagement with the University of Iowa, support and advance the university and its programs through meaningful pre-professional opportunities, and support potential graduates to obtain roles within our organization.

The UICA will provide 9 intern opportunities that provide 10 weeks of work experience, June 1 - August 6. Internships are open to students entering their second year of college in Fall 2027 through students graduating from any college or university in 2027. Interns will earn $18/hour and will be provided with the flexibility and technology to work from home two days per week if desired. Up to five unpaid vacation days will be available throughout the internship program if desired. At the conclusion of the internship, all interns are expected to give a final presentation highlighting their experience and projects they have worked on. Housing and benefits are not available as part of the intern experience and interns must be within driving distance of our Iowa City, IA office.

As the Alumni Engagement Intern, you will support initiatives that strengthen connections between the University of Iowa and its alumni community. Working alongside Alumni Engagement professionals, you will contribute to projects that engage current alumni, foster connections with future alumni, and explore innovative strategies for reaching Hawkeyes who are not yet actively involved. This internship will provide hands-on experience in event planning, alumni relations, community engagement, outreach strategy, and program assessment. Through research, direct engagement, and collaborative projects, you will gain valuable insight into how meaningful alumni experiences help advance lifelong connections with the University of Iowa.

Core Responsibilities

  • Assist with the planning, coordination, execution, and evaluation of alumni and friends events, including communications, registration, logistics, and on-site support.
  • Conduct research and benchmarking of alumni engagement programs and best practices across Big Ten and peer institutions, and present findings and recommendations.
  • Support outreach and engagement initiatives designed to increase alumni participation, strengthen university connections, and reach new or previously unengaged audiences.
  • Collaborate with Alumni Engagement staff on special projects and strategic priorities, contributing research, analysis, project updates, and recommendations.
  • Engage directly with alumni and friends at programs such as RAGBRAI and Grandparents University, providing exceptional customer service and representing the University of Iowa professionally.

Qualifications

title: At Your Service Center Associate, Southern Park Mall - Part Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As an At Your Service Center Colleague, you are at the heart of delivering a seamless and personalized shopping experience. You’ll support all At Your Service activities, including Buy Online Pickup In Store (BOPS), merchandise returns, order pickups, and other assigned tasks - all while upholding Macy’s service standards.

This role requires strong multitasking abilities, problem-solving, attention to detail, and a customer-first mindset. You’ll thrive in a fast-paced environment where flexibility is key, including working a variety of shifts such as nights, weekends, and holidays.

This role goes far beyond just being a cashier. Here, the customer is at the heart of everything we do - every day, all day. If you're passionate about selling, reaching goals, working as a team, and creating amazing experiences through genuine hospitality, this could be the perfect fit for you! You’ll also help keep the shopping space clean, organized, and inviting so every customer feels welcome the moment they walk in.

How Our At Your Service Colleagues Spend Their Day…

  • Every day starts with a positive example. As an At Your Service Colleagues (AYS), you come in energized and ready to make an impact - wearing your name badge with pride, greeting teammates with warmth, and helping ensure the At Your Service areas is clean, organized, and ready for customers. You help set the pace by reviewing sales goals, learning about new arrivals and top-selling items, and staying up to date on trends and promotions - so you’re prepared to support the team and engage customers confidently.
  • In the At Your Service area, you lead through action - welcoming customers with genuine hospitality, making eye contact, and starting friendly, personal conversations that build lasting relationships. Assist customers in all aspects of total store fulfillment, including By Online and Pick Up in Store, be proficient in all systems needed to complete transactions, and ensure the collection area is organized so the customer pick-up experience is friction-free
  • You help maintain a shoppable space by recovering merchandise and keeping the pickup and return areas clean while ensuring timely completion and curbside delivery of Buy Online Pickup In Store (BOPS) orders.
  • They always Finish Strong - sharing our Loyalty program benefits, making sure customers have all they need, and ending with a sincere thank-you, often walking the package around and using the customer’s name.
  • We believe service starts with each other - supporting one another with honesty, care, and collaboration so we can better serve our customers and communities.
  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

Who You Are

  • Flexible availability, including days, evenings, weekends and holidays with regular, dependable attendance and punctuality
  • Must be able to:
    • Understand and communicate effectively with customers, co-workers, and supervisors
    • Read and understand employment policies and safety rules/procedures in English
  • Makes prompt, sound decisions in real time to effectively address customer needs and resolve issues
  • Be comfortable communicating and collaborating with customers and colleagues
  • Meeting daily sales goal challenges
  • Responsible for acquiring new customers by opening credit accounts and sharing loyalty benefits
  • Enjoy meeting people, learning about them, and sharing information
  • Resourceful and eager to start a new venture and can adapt to changing priorities; you can work on your own but are great with team dynamics
  • You can handle electronic devices with no problem

Essential Physical Requirements You Will Perform

  • This position requires talking, lifting, constant moving, standing, and reaching with arms and hands.
  • Standing for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 25lbs. stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders, reaching, including above eye level.
  • Requires close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment.
  • Frequent use of computers and other technology, necessary to perform job functions, including handheld equipment, cash register and ability to process register transactions.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!

Minimum Qualifications

The minimum qualifications for a Store Manager are:

  • High School diploma or GED preferred.
  • Experience in retail sales preferred.
  • Experience to perform the essential duties, responsibilities and working in the conditions described below.
  • Ability to supervise and train for the use of equipment, tools and materials listed in the Customer Service Representative (CSR) and Assistant Site Manager (ASM) job description.
  • Ability to supervise and manage the functions listed in the CSR and ASM job description.
  • Ability to use computer, or acquire those skills necessary to use a computer at the site, which includes analysis of reports, inventory control, cash control, counseling notices, etc.
  • A valid driver’s license and adequate transportation to/from bank and corporate management meetings.
  • Ability to communicate (orally and in writing) in English.
  • Perform other duties as assigned or delegated by his/her supervisor.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES, RESPONSIBILITIES AND SKILLS

Leadership and Management

  • Recruit, hire and train positive, enthusiastic employees, ensuring excellent customer service.
  • Develop, manage and assign tasks appropriately to ensure the site is clean, adequately stocked, organize and well kept based on Company standards.
  • Maintain a professional and supportive image among subordinates and supervisor.
  • Schedule employees within Company guidelines to maximize customer service and maintain site image.
  • Implement non-discriminatory related management skills while hiring, training, counseling, motivating and separating employees.

Site Relationships

  • Develop positive and professional relationships with all suppliers.
  • Promote excellent service and resolve customer complaints in a timely, professional manner.
  • Promote and ensure a safe, positive public image within the neighboring community.

Training and Development

  • Prepare on-going and timely performance appraisals in writing for all employees, providing proper performance based feedback.
  • Train all employees ensuring that customer service, site image and marketing execution meet Company standards.
  • Train all employees on safety procedures and promote safety awareness.

Communication

  • Develop ways and means to ensure that all employees receive proper communication in a timely manner.
  • Establish periodic on-going communication meetings with all site employees and the Market Manager.

Organizing and Planning

  • Evaluate and develop specific action plans to address the needs of the site in order to reach the desired objectives.
  • Organize and maintain all site files and manuals.
  • Manage and supervise store employees to ensure that all required and requested reports due are completed accurately and timely.
  • Manage and supervise store employees to ensure that all merchandise is stocked, attractively displayed and priced correctly.
  • Ensure that all required employment related posters and signs are in a place that is easily accessible to all employees.

Financial

  • Analyze daily sales and expense information and take appropriate action to maximize sales and net profits.
  • Budget and forecast P&L lines, as well as understand and manage merchandise margins.
  • Safeguard and account for all money received and disbursed.
  • Perform all other financial analysis necessary to maximize sales and net profits.

Working Conditions

  • Performs approximately all work indoors but will be required to work outside in order to clean parking lots, gas pumps, take out garbage, etc.
  • Be exposed to occasional cold temperature extremes while supervising or managing store employees performing occasional work in a walk-in cooler and/or freezer.
  • Be exposed to occasional noise.
  • Work with a minimum of direction and supervision.
  • At all times work as an effective manager, supervisor and leader.

title: NSF NOIRLab Director
description:
The Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy (AURA) is seeking an accomplished scientific leader and executive to serve as the next Director of the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) National Optical-Infrared Astronomy Research Laboratory (NSF NOIRLab). In this emerging era of extremely large datasets and time-domain astrophysics, the Director will shepherd and promote NOIRLab as a world-class scientific and technological resource for the astronomy research community. This pivotal role requires a candidate with a proven track record of managing large, complex scientific or technical organizations. The incoming Director will be charged with advancing merit-driven science across an integrated system of data and observing facilities.

The incoming Director will champion NOIRLab’s vision for astronomy in the 2030s: to enable scientific discoveries that would otherwise be impossible. The Director is responsible for building an integrated national astronomy ecosystem by connecting advanced observing capabilities, expanding access to data products and analysis tools, and modernizing operations across geographically dispersed facilities. By optimizing shared infrastructure and expertise across the organization, the successful candidate will position NOIRLab as a central hub for community-driven science—building innovative scientific programs, accelerating the exchange of ideas, and enabling transformative breakthroughs in our understanding of the universe.

NOIRLab is driven by a sophisticated, multidisciplinary workforce of nearly 600 FTEs, spanning scientific, technical, and engineering disciplines, as well as specialized expertise in project management, communications, education and outreach, finance, and business administration. The incoming Director must skillfully lead this dynamic organization, align operational priorities, and foster a cohesive organizational culture across matrixed, geographically distributed teams in Arizona, Hawaiʻi, and Chile.

General Description of Position:

The NOIRLab Director, reporting through the AURA President to the AURA Board of Directors, is responsible for NOIRLab’s strategic, scientific, operational, and managerial leadership. This includes defining NOIRLab’s vision and structure; setting priorities and establishing goals across the organization and its programs; and providing leadership, guidance, oversight, and support to the NOIRLab senior management team and staff across the organization. The NOIRLab Director is responsible for working with partners and stakeholders within the broad national and international research community to ensure existing and future programs are conducted successfully and drive scientific innovation.

The Director will work primarily from a NOIRLab location in Tucson, Arizona; Hilo, Hawaiʻi; or La Serena, Chile, with frequent travel to other locations.

The Director will be selected through an open competition, with a targeted start by October 1, 2027.

About NOIRLab

NSF NOIRLab is the preeminent U.S. national center for ground-based, nighttime optical and infrared astronomy. NOIRLab’s mission is to enable breakthrough discoveries in astrophysics by developing and operating state-of-the-art ground-based observatories and providing data products and services for the astronomical community.

NOIRLab operates the following programs in collaboration with federal, national, and international entities:

  • NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory
  • International Gemini Observatory
  • Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory
  • Kitt Peak National Observatory
  • Community Science Data Center

NOIRLab’s open-access facilities and data pipelines enable data-intensive and community-driven research across all scales of astrophysics—from cosmological studies of dark energy and dark matter to galactic evolution, exoplanetary systems, and planetary science within our own Solar System.

As a Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC), NOIRLab provides the U.S. Government with long-term, independent, and objective scientific, technical, and analytical expertise that cannot be met by other means. As such, close coordination and collaboration with NSF, as the primary funding agency, is an important role the NOIRLab Director must fulfill in collaboration with AURA’s corporate leadership.

About AURA

AURA manages world-class facilities and science to enable the next decade of astronomical discoveries by providing access and opportunities for all astronomers. Our 1700 highly skilled professionals—located across the continental United States, Hawaiʻi, and Chile—build, operate, and support state-of-the-art facilities, data centers, and science platforms. On behalf of U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), we manage NSF NOIRLab and NSF National Solar Observatory (including the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope). On behalf of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), we manage the Space Telescope Science Institute, which is the science operations center for the Hubble and Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescopes and the science and mission operations center for the James Webb Space Telescope.

Essential Functions:

  • Innovate, motivate and drive forward the NOIRLab mission, in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Develop and implement NOIRLab strategic plans, initiatives, budgets, and priorities.
  • Develop and sustain critical relationships across federal funding agencies, international scientific partnerships, complex labor environments, and regional host communities; seek strategic collaborations and advocate for the NOIRLab mission and strategic plan.
  • Oversee complex and distributed operations of national and international multi-user observing facilities and data science platforms.
  • Ensure the effectiveness, integration, and alignment of NOIRLab leadership; motivate and build employee trust, competencies, and agility across the organization.
  • Facilitate and lead effective change management to ensure NOIRLab delivers against current requirements and future needs.
  • Collaborate effectively with AURA’s President, corporate leaders, and the Board to address key efforts, risks, challenges, and opportunities.
  • Interact directly with NSF, the U.S. Department of Energy, and other funding organizations to steward substantial federal investments in astronomy research and education.
  • Collaborate with the AURA Leadership Team to enhance AURA’s mission and the combined scientific impacts of its federally funded research capabilities.
  • Serve as the Principal Investigator (PI/co-PI) by overseeing scientific, technical, and budgetary aspects of NOIRLab’s projects and operations, including working with other AURA staff to prepare NSF and other funding proposals.
  • Work with the NOIRLab Deputy Director, members of the NOIRLab senior leadership team, and AURA Corporate to champion the institutional safety, operational excellence, and long-term scientific mission of the Lab.

Required Education/Experience/Skills/Abilities:

  • Ph.D. in Astronomy, Astrophysics, or a closely related scientific or engineering discipline.
  • Track record of success in an executive leadership role managing complex, international, and/or geographically distributed astronomy projects or major facilities.
  • Extensive experience in strategic planning, multi-agency budgetary planning and oversight, and complex financial management.
  • Demonstrated excellence in conflict resolution, critical analysis, and operational problem solving within a matrixed workforce.
  • Direct experience leading successful organizational change management and/or institutional restructuring.
  • Proven ability to balance and prioritize competing requirements from multiple stakeholders.
  • Exceptional interpersonal, diplomatic, and communication skills with a demonstrated ability to build, lead, and unify diverse, high-performing teams.

Preferred Education/Experience/Skills/Abilities:

  • Experience overseeing programs utilizing large-scale datasets, data management systems, or time-domain astrophysics workflows.
  • Experience managing the lifecycle, development, and/or maintenance of complex hardware and software systems.
  • A strong commitment to, and track record of, scientific community engagement, supporting regional host communities, educational outreach, and workforce development.
  • Deep knowledge of federal funding agency strategies, policies, and performance metrics.

Salary

The final salary will depend on skills, qualifications, experience and job location.

description:
Hej Digital Platform Leader for Agentic Retail

Inter IKEA Group connects IKEA franchisees with range development and suppliers and ensures alignment of the overall IKEA strategic direction. Every day, we strive to develop, produce, and sell products and services that are affordable and accessible to everyone.

This role is positioned in Retail Concept Operations. You will belong to the Retail Digital Operations team, reporting to the Platform Area Manager.

In Retail Concept Operations, as part of Retail Concept, we protect, develop, and enable the IKEA Concept across markets and franchisees. We turn the 'what' of the IKEA Concept into the 'how' of everyday retail operations, making it easy to use, scale, and trust across the value chain.

We take pride in working in progressive ways of working, with empowered teams and strong digital competence. We focus on simple, practical solutions that strengthen both short- and long-term low cost, while supporting consistency and quality in how the IKEA Concept comes to life.

Together, we build ways of working where teams take ownership, collaborate closely, and continuously improve, so we can create meaningful value for IKEA, our franchisees, co-workers, and the many people.

Our team enables digital platforms that support the IKEA Concept across markets and franchisees, making it easier for products, services and teams to work together in a secure, scalable and reliable way. Together, we continuously improve developer experience and platform capabilities to create value across the IKEA value chain.

Our team is based in Malmö. We believe that your presence with the team and working the majority of the time in the workplace is important.

About the role

You will shape the platform that enables the next generation of agentic retail operations across IKEA and our franchisees. Combining strategic thinking with hands-on leadership, you will define its vision and roadmap, align with internal enabling functions and advance capabilities in the Microsoft ecosystem, including Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry and Agent 365. A central challenge is enabling agents to work together across our internal and retail tenants and retailers' separate tenants, with clear security and data boundaries. Working closely with developers, product teams, architects and suppliers, you will turn emerging opportunities into practical platform capabilities while ensuring operational excellence and continuous improvement. This is an exciting opportunity for a co-worker with experience in digital product, platform or technology development to take the next step in platform leadership and support IKEA's digital transformation journey.

You will lead a team that combines platform engineering with hands-on support to the business. Two Forward Deployed Engineers work directly inside the product teams in the capability area Retail Commercial and Customer, helping them find valuable use cases, build their first agents and move from experiment to production. Your job is to make that support repeatable: turn what the engineers learn into reusable capabilities, patterns and platform improvements, and align these with internal enabling functions so teams can adopt them consistently. By connecting practical retail needs with shared platform capabilities, you will help our work create lasting value in homes and hearts across the world.

On a typical working day, you will:

  • Define and communicate the platform vision, roadmap and priorities to stakeholders and platform users.
  • Lead backlog management, release planning and prioritisation to ensure the platform delivers value to developers and digital products.
  • Collaborate with product teams, architects, suppliers and developers to remove dependencies, solve challenges and continuously improve platform capabilities.

What we'd like you to bring to the table

The role as a Digital Platform Leader requires you to:

  • Have experience in digital product, platform or software development, ideally within agile or DevOps environments, and be able to turn emerging AI and agent capabilities into reusable solutions that teams can take from experimentation to production.
  • Demonstrate a strong understanding of developer needs and software engineering practices.
  • Lead through collaboration, creating alignment across teams, stakeholders and suppliers.
  • Make informed decisions using both qualitative and quantitative data.
  • Communicate effectively with technical and business audiences and translate complexity into simple, actionable outcomes.
  • Drive continuous improvement and deliver results in a fast-moving digital environment.
  • Be fluent in spoken and written English.

It's a plus if you also:

  • Have experience building or managing internal platforms, developer platforms or shared technology capabilities.
  • Have experience with platform performance measurement, operational excellence and service management.
  • Bring knowledge of modern technology landscapes, cloud platforms or digital ecosystem development.

We welcome your application

We look forward to receiving your application by the 20th October 2026 at the latest. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

If you have any questions about the role or the recruitment process, or if you have a special need that requires accommodation in the recruitment process, feel free to contact the Recruiter Jordi Menick (jordi.menick@inter.ikea.com)

We always recruit based on values, competence, potential and diversity. Once competence requirements are met, we will first consider impacted co-workers employed in Inter IKEA Systems Service AB, Inter IKEA Technology Services AB and Inter IKEA Systems BV and secondly impacted co-workers at Inter IKEA Group.

Please note that this job posting is intended only for candidates who have been selected by Fox Rothschild to interview for this position as part of the Drexel University Co-op Program. Applications received from candidates who do not meet these criteria will be disregarded.

The Legal Talent Management Intern will work closely with various members of the Legal Talent Management Department in support of the Firm’s Attorney Recruitment efforts.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Provide support for the Attorney Recruiting operations.
  • Assist with entering candidate materials and updating candidate statuses in database as candidates move through the interview process.
  • Assist with scheduling candidate interviews.
  • Manage and ship recruitment materials.
  • Unpack post-event items and restock reusable materials.
  • Contribute to event preparation.
  • Conduct research on new event venues and giveaway items.
  • Help generate reports and assist with maintaining accurate recruitment data.
  • Maintain search firm agreements and handle processing invoice payments.
  • Support the planning and execution of new attorney and paralegal orientation, including ordering equipment and sending calendar appointments and confirmation emails.
  • Assist with coordinating meetings for the attorney recruitment team including scheduling, submitting video conference and hospitality requests, booking conference rooms, and preparing materials.
  • Communicate with multiple departments across the Firm.
  • Assist with various administrative duties and special projects as needed.

QUALIFICATIONS (EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES):

  • Some related recruitment or human resources experience/second or final Co-op preferred
  • Strong verbal, written and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to handle multiple assignments simultaneously.
  • Strong administrative skills (typing, phone manners, etc.).
  • Strong computer skills to manage various candidate tracking and budget spreadsheets and databases.
  • Proficiency with Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, etc.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to work well in a team environment.

WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • This job operates in a clerical, office setting. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines.

DISCLAIMER

Fox Rothschild LLP is under no obligation to provide sponsorship for this position. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis now and in the future.

title: SC32P3 Information Scientist
description:
CAS uses intuitive technology, unparalleled scientific content, and unmatched human expertise to help companies create groundbreaking innovations that benefit the world. As the scientific information solutions division of the American Chemical Society, CAS manages the largest curated reservoir of scientific knowledge, and for over 119 years, has helped innovators mine, assess, and apply that information to keep businesses thriving. The CAS team is global, diverse, and endlessly curious, and strives to make scientific insights accessible to innovators worldwide.

CAS is currently seeking an Information Scientist on our Content Operations team. This position will be located in our Columbus, OH headquarters.

Position Summary

We are seeking a technically strong Information Scientist to advance computational chemistry initiatives within our organization. This role combines deep scientific expertise with software development skills to drive innovation in chemical information processing and molecular modeling. Comfort using AI-assisted tools in scientific workflows is important, as these tools are increasingly central to how we approach chemistry problems.

You will work closely with cross-functional teams of scientists and developers to design scalable solutions and deepen our chemistry domain capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Apply computational chemistry techniques to model stereochemistry, coordination chemistry, and molecular interactions.
  • Design and implement reusable frameworks for chemical data processing, search, and visualization.
  • Use AI-assisted tools and approaches to support chemical structure recognition, reaction analysis, and related curation workflows.
  • Stay current on emerging AI capabilities relevant to chemistry and assess their fit and accuracy for specific scientific applications.
  • Collaborate with product owners, subject matter experts, and developers to groom backlogs and deliver solutions in Agile environments.
  • Contribute to a culture of scientific rigor, collaboration, and continuous learning across the team.

Qualifications

  • PhD or Master’s degree in Chemistry, Computational Chemistry, or a related field (candidates with another four-year degree and exceptional experience may be considered).
  • 5+ years of experience in computational chemistry or scientific software engineering.
  • Strong programming skills in Java, Python, and JavaScript, with familiarity with cheminformatics libraries such as RDKit and Open Babel.
  • Comfortable using AI tools (e.g., LLM-based assistants, structure recognition tools) to support scientific and curation work.
  • Deep understanding of stereochemistry, coordination chemistry, and molecular modeling.
  • Experience with connection table algorithms and chemical structure processing, through development or research work.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across scientific and technical teams.
  • Strong communication, analytical reasoning, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience evaluating or validating AI-generated outputs (e.g., structure recognition, reaction extraction) against scientific ground truth.
  • Curiosity about how AI tools are reshaping chemistry workflows, with a track record of adopting new tools effectively.

CAS offers a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package, including a generous vacation plan, medical, dental, vision insurance plans, and employee savings and retirement plans. Candidates for this position must be authorized to work in the United States and not require work authorization sponsorship by our company for this position now or in the future. title: Vil du jobbe med salg og kundeopplevelser på IKEA Leangen?
description:
Har du en lidenskap for interiør, elsker å møte mennesker og motiveres av å skape gode resultater? Da kan dette være muligheten for deg!

Vi søker nå en butikkmedarbeider i en 20 % fast stilling på IKEA Leangen. Som en del av salgsteamet vil du bidra til å skape inspirerende handleopplevelser og hjelpe kundene våre med å finne smarte løsninger for hjemmet sitt.

Hos IKEA blir du en del av et inkluderende og verdidrevet arbeidsmiljø hvor samarbeid, utvikling og fellesskap står sentralt. Du får muligheten til å lære mer om salg, kundeopplevelser og innredning, samtidig som du bidrar til å gjøre IKEA til førstevalget for de mange menneskene.

Hva skal du gjøre fra dag til dag

Som butikkmedarbeider vil du møte kunder gjennom hele kjøpsreisen. Du gir råd, veileder og inspirerer, samtidig som du sikrer at vareområdet fremstår attraktivt, kommersielt og salgsfremmende. Du vil samarbeide tett med kolleger på tvers av varehusets avdelinger og bidra til at vi når våre mål innen salg, kundetilfredshet og kundeopplevelse.

Hvem er du?

Det er viktig at du er nysgjerrig og ønsker å skape en bedre hverdag for de mange menneskene som besøker oss. I tillegg ser vi etter deg som:

• Er fokusert og engasjert, og er til stede i jobben når du er på.
• Er glad i å selge og motiveres av å skape resultater.
• Er positiv, utadvendt og uredd i møte med kunder.
• Trives i et høyt tempo og tar initiativ når det er mye å gjøre.
• Er pålitelig, ansvarsbevisst og selvgående.
•Har gode kommunikasjonsevner og evner å bygge relasjoner med kunder og kolleger.
•Har et kommersielt blikk og forstår verdien av gode kundeopplevelser.
• Har en genuin lidenskap for interiør og hjeminnredning.

Har du spørsmål om rollen eller ønsker å vite mer om hverdagen på IKEA, er du velkommen til å kontakte Siw Anita Hopmo på siwanita.hopmo@ingka.ikea.com.
